Job Description

Schedule: Monday - Thursday, 5pm-9pm (16 hours per week)

Position Summary:

The Kitchen Worker provides operational support for a high-volume operation while ensuring proper sanitation, efficient practices, and compliance with food handling standards. The Kitchen Worker provides a wide range of support including, but not limited to food preparation, dish and ware washing, maintaining cleanliness and trash removal, serving food, and stocking as necessary. This position is part of the success of the food service program serving food through dining halls, cafes, catering, and a food truck. The Kitchen Worker follows Health Department regulations and expectations of Vassar College with regards to food quality, safety, preparation, presentation, and audit compliance.

Responsibilities:

  • As directed by the management team, complete tasks that contribute to the Dining Services daily operation.

  • Perform quality work and meet deadlines for meals as assigned by the culinary and management teams.

  • Assemble salads and sandwiches using pre-cooked or ready-to-eat ingredients, prepare protein-based salads such as tuna salad, and chop, organize, and prepare ingredients to be used for service or for the overall food production effort.

  • Properly and safely use various knives to cut and prepare food ingredients with precision and efficiency

  • Serve food according to food safety guidelines and monitor for freshness and quality.

  • Understanding of FIFO principles with daily rotation of stock and properly date/label products stored in coolers, dry storage, or kitchen areas in proper storage containers.

  • Capacity to operate all of the stations and platforms throughout the dining operation within classification.

  • As the runner, gather ingredients and ice from coolers, freezers and stock rooms for efficient food production and service.

  • Throughout the duration of a shift, at the conclusion of a shift, and in preparation for service the next day, ensure kitchen surfaces including floors as well as equipment, pots, pans and utensils dishes, and flatware are maintained, cleaned, sanitized, and organized appropriately to expected standards.

  • Responsible for the proper use of the dish room equipment using water softener and dish washing chemical disbursement to clean, scrape, wash, and stack dishes, utensils, and cooking equipment.

  • Execute utility functions such as, but not limited to sweeping, mopping, cleaning up spills, trash removal, compostable collection, breaking down boxes, proper collection of recyclables including cardboard, and cleaning and sanitizing carts and trash receptacles and trash collection areas as needed.

  • Clean and sanitize stations, tables, and counters throughout the operation. Restock dishes, flatware, pots, pans, cups, glasses and utensils. Refill napkin baskets, condiments, and salt/pepper shakers as needed.

  • Make coffee and refill milks, sweeteners, juices, soda, C02, and ensure the beverage areas remain clean and sanitary.

  • Restock open air coolers and serving areas with product, fruit, and other items as needed. Assist with putting chairs on tables at the end of the night.

  • Operate and safely use equipment necessary for the job including dish room equipment, assigned kitchen equipment and elevators.

Required knowledge, skills and abilities:

  • Ability to lift heavy objects up to 50 pounds and frequently lift and push, pull or carry up to 30 pounds. Team lift anything greater than 50 pounds.

  • Ability to stand and walk for the duration of a shift using repetitive motion with your upper body to complete tasks.

  • Communicate effectively in English including understanding speaking, reading and writing.

  • Remain within work deployment for the duration of a shift except for scheduled breaks and meal periods.

  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with staff, students/customers, and management. Serve customers in an efficient and friendly manner while resolving any potential issues, remaining flexible to last minute adjustments, and/or by promptly reporting issues to management.

  • Must help ensure success of the dining program by following Health Department regulations and food safety standards as laid out by Vassar and Vassar’s food contract management company.

  • Use necessary protective equipment per guidelines from Vassar and Vassar’s food contract management company.

  • Properly direct and refer questions as it relates to HACCP principles in the field of sanitation and cooking, and allergen and celiac disease.

Preferred knowledge, skills and abilities:

  • 1 year of professional food service experience in a high-volume food service environment.

  • Certification in the National Restaurant Association’s ServSafe course for food safety.

  • Willingness to work overtime when available, as assigned according to seniority guidelines.

Pay Rate: $21.39 per hour

title: Network Engineer I
description:
Job Description

The Network Engineer is responsible for the design, development, optimization, security, performance, reliability, and ongoing support of Wentworth Institute of Technology’s wired and wireless network infrastructure. This role manages the full lifecycle of network devices and systems, including routers, switches, firewalls, cabling, wireless access points, and controllers. Key responsibilities include planning, designing, and implementing network infrastructure projects, working both independently and collaboratively with cross-functional teams. This involves engaging stakeholders to gather requirements, coordinating internal and external resources, developing and presenting network designs, overseeing project implementation, and maintaining comprehensive network documentation.

Reporting to the Director of IT Infrastructure and Security, the Network Engineer works closely with the Information Security Officer and IT Security team to ensure compliance with security best practices. This includes utilizing tools such as Network Access Control (NAC) to develop, implement, and enforce security policies and controls across the wired and wireless network environment.

Essential Functions

  • Design, implement, and optimize wired and wireless network infrastructure for the Wentworth campus, including all residential, academic, and service buildings, including both new network installations and the refresh of existing network installations with new technology.

  • Serve as a technical point of contact for any university projects that include a networking component.

  • Ensure that the design implemented optimizes the network experience of students, faculty, and staff while providing a highly redundant, secure, and reliable network infrastructure.

  • Respond to, troubleshoot, and resolve any network related issues or problem.

  • Proactively identify potential network problems using the network monitoring and analysis tools available and develop and implement plans to remediate issues.

  • Review incident tickets and respond to client requests and issues in a timely fashion and with a high level of customer service.

  • Develop documentation and training for both the Tech Spot and for end users to provide faster resolution of common issues and to optimize the use of the network.

  • Implement, optimize, and maintain network monitoring and alerting applications and tools.

  • Monitor the usage, capacity, and reliability of various network related systems and plan steps needed to resolve issues and sustain the network infrastructure for current and future applications.

  • Identify utilization patterns and their effects on Internet traffic and plan effective ways to maintain the highest quality of service possible.

  • Maintain network monitoring and management system and ensure reporting is accurate.

  • Create, update, and maintain design documentation of all network systems, including but not limited to structured cabling, wiring closets, network switches and routers, wireless APs and controllers.

  • Create knowledge base documentation for common network related issues or procedures, as well as training documentation for first level Tech Spot support staff and for other network support staff.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field, or a combination of education, relevant work experience, and professional certifications—such as industry-recognized credentials or international degree equivalencies—may be accepted in place of a bachelor’s degree.

  • Minimum 3-5 years of relative experience implementing and supporting critical network infrastructure and technology.

  • In depth understanding of Local Area Network (LAN) and Wide Area Network (WAN) technologies and protocols.

  • In depth understanding of wireless networking protocols and standards (802.11).

  • Experience implementing, optimizing, and maintaining network monitoring and alerting applications and tools.

  • Experience working on a technical team, collaborating with other teams and departments, and providing guidance and leadership to other technical team members.

  • Demonstrated record of providing a high level of customer service for end users and responding to any interruption of service with an appropriate sense of urgency.

  • Demonstrated knowledge of Internet of Things (IOT) devices and terminology. Experience supporting and implementing them on an enterprise network.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Minimum of 5+ years of relative experience implementing and supporting critical network infrastructure and technology.

  • Experience deploying and supporting HP/Aruba routers and switches.

  • Experience deploying and supporting HP/Aruba wireless access points, mobility controllers, and network access control (Clearpass).

  • Experience in developing implementation plans and network designs for refreshing network hardware and incorporating new technologies.

  • Experience designing, analyzing, optimizing, and troubleshooting Wi-Fi networks.

  • Ability to present technical information clearly and understandably to a diverse set of individuals and groups on campus.

  • Experience with Palo Alto Networks firewalls.

  • Familiarity with higher education-specific networking needs (dense residential deployments, IoT support, research networks).

  • Knowledge of multi-ISP environments and hybrid cloud connectivity.

  • Certifications such as Aruba Certified Switching Professional (ACSP), Aruba ClearPass Certified, Palo Alto PCNSA/PCNSE, CCNA, or equivalent.

Work Environment

While this position is often office-based and sedentary, the Network Engineer must regularly move throughout buildings, offices, data center space, and telecommunication closet to install, inspect, troubleshoot and maintain network equipment. The role may often require lifting or carrying equipment or tools weighing up to 20 pounds.

Position Details

The job grade for this position is Grade 8.

The expected salary for this position is between $78,000 - $98,000 which reflects what we reasonably expect to pay for this role.

At this time, the university is unable to sponsor applicants for H-1B visas for this position.

This position is a 37.5-hour work week schedule. This is an in-person position that requires the incumbent to be on site daily. This position is not eligible for remote work.

Compensation and Benefits

Wentworth Institute of Technology is committed to fair, transparent, and legally compliant compensation practices. We believe that clarity about pay structures and ranges supports equity, fosters trust, and ensures a positive workplace for all employees.

Please visit here to see the comprehensive benefits package offered to support the best experience for our employees.

Inclusive Excellence at Wentworth

Inclusive Excellence is one of the four pillars of the Strategic Plan. Actively and intentionally cultivating a diverse and culturally competent institution where each member has the opportunity and support to reach their full potential and make contributions to our campus community and beyond is Inclusive Excellence at Wentworth.

To find out more about the Wentworth’s commitment to Inclusive Excellence, please visit the website .

All applicants have the right to accessibility support and accommodations. To request accessibility support or accommodations, contact the Executive Director of Equity and Compliance, Catlin Wells, at wellsc1@wit.edu.

E-Verify for Employment Eligibility Verification (Form I-9)

Wentworth participates in E-Verify. E-Verify is an internet-based system that compares information from your Form I-9 to records available to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Social Security Administration (SSA) to confirm that you are authorized to work in the United States.

title: Lead Managed Services Consultant
description:
Sprinklr is the definitive, AI-native platform for Unified Customer Experience Management (Unified-CXM), empowering brands to deliver extraordinary experiences at scale — across every customer touchpoint.

By combining human instinct with the speed and efficiency of AI, Sprinklr helps brands earn trust and loyalty through personalized, seamless, and efficient customer interactions. Sprinklr’s unified platform provides powerful solutions for every customer-facing team — spanning social media management, marketing, advertising, customer feedback, and omnichannel contact center management — enabling enterprises to unify data, break down silos, and act on real-time insights.

Today, 1,900+ enterprises and 60% of the Fortune 100 rely on Sprinklr to help them deliver consistent, trusted customer experiences worldwide.

Job Description

Role Summary

Lead managed services delivery for Sprinklr Community customers by owning the strategy, architecture, governance, and evolution of customer community platforms. Drive community transformation initiatives, user experience optimization, platform adoption, and operational excellence while serving as the primary advisor to customers on community best practices, digital engagement, and platform roadmap execution.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead end-to-end management and optimization of Sprinklr Community platforms, ensuring scalability, performance, governance, and business alignment.

  • Design and oversee community architecture including forums, discussion boards, knowledge communities, user journeys, moderation frameworks, gamification, and engagement models.

  • Act as the primary strategic advisor for customer community initiatives, providing recommendations on platform adoption, engagement growth, governance, and operational maturity.

  • Drive requirements discovery, solution design, roadmap planning, and execution of community enhancement programs.

  • Define and implement community governance frameworks including roles, permissions, moderation strategies, content lifecycle management, and user access controls.

  • Lead root cause analysis and resolution of complex platform, workflow, configuration, and user experience issues.

  • Own community analytics, adoption reporting, engagement insights, and continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Provide leadership and guidance to consultants and technical teams supporting community operations and managed services delivery.

  • Partner with Customer Success, Product, Engineering, and customer leadership teams to ensure successful outcomes and long-term platform value realization.

  • Lead release management, platform audits, health checks, optimization reviews, and best practice assessments.

  • Oversee UI/UX strategy and front-end customization initiatives to deliver intuitive, accessible, and engaging community experiences.

  • Provide architectural guidance on API integrations, SSO, CRM connectivity, and third-party ecosystem integrations.

  • Establish reusable governance models, operational playbooks, implementation standards, and community best practices.

What Makes You Qualified?

Must Have Qualifications

  • 8-12 years of experience in Community Platforms, Digital Experience Platforms, Managed Services, SaaS Consulting, or Customer Engagement solutions.

  • Deep hands-on experience with Sprinklr Community or similar platforms such as Khoros, Gainsight, Salesforce Experience Cloud, Higher Logic, or Enterprise Community solutions.

  • Proven experience designing, building, launching, and managing large-scale customer community portals and online forums.

  • Strong expertise in community architecture, moderation frameworks, engagement strategies, governance models, and digital customer experiences.

  • Advanced knowledge of UI/UX principles, information architecture, user journey design, accessibility, and community experience optimization.

  • Strong understanding of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, responsive design principles, and front-end customization approaches.

  • High-level understanding of REST APIs, authentication models, SSO, webhooks, integrations, and enterprise system connectivity.

  • Experience leading customer workshops, solution design sessions, governance reviews, and executive stakeholder discussions.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, consulting, and customer management capabilities.

Good to Have Skills

  • Experience with customer support communities, brand advocacy programs, knowledge communities, or peer-to-peer support ecosystems.

  • Exposure to SEO, search optimization, content strategy, and digital engagement best practices.

  • Understanding of CRM platforms, customer support ecosystems, and customer experience technologies.

  • Experience managing globally distributed communities and enterprise-scale engagement programs.

  • Program management and service delivery leadership experience within managed services organizations.

Who You Are

  • A strategic consultant with deep expertise in customer communities and digital engagement platforms.

  • Passionate about building world-class community experiences that drive adoption, engagement, and business outcomes.

  • Comfortable engaging with both executive stakeholders and technical teams.

  • A thought leader who combines consulting, technical, operational, and design expertise to deliver customer success.

  • Driven by continuous improvement, innovation, and long-term customer value realization.

What Success Looks Like

  • Highly engaged, scalable, and well-governed customer communities.

  • Strong customer satisfaction, adoption, and business value realization.

  • Successful execution of strategic community transformation and optimization initiatives.

  • Improved user experience, engagement metrics, and operational efficiency.

  • Trusted advisor status with customer leadership and key stakeholders.

  • Consistent delivery of managed services KPIs, governance objectives, and platform growth outcomes.

We focus on our mission: Sprinklr was founded in 2009 to solve a big problem: growing enterprise complexity that separated brands from their customers. Our vision was clear: to unify fragmented teams, tools and data — helping large organizations build deeper, more meaningful connections with the people they serve. Today, Sprinklr has a unified, AI-native platform for four product suites: Sprinklr Service, Sprinklr Social, Sprinklr Marketing, and Sprinklr Insights. Sprinklr is here to do three things:

  • Lead a new category of enterprise software that we call Unified-CXM.

  • Empower companies to deliver next generation, unified engagement journeys that reimagine the customer experience.

  • Create a culture of customer obsession, with trust, teamwork, and accountability.

We believe in our product: Customers who value exceptional customer experiences have what they need on our single unified platform, built with an operating system approach on a single codebase. That means that everything — and everyone — can work together to service, respond, sell, and market to customers on the channels they prefer. While Unified Customer Experience Management (Unified-CXM) as a category is just getting started, we are well on our way to creating a no-compromise, unified approach to better customer experiences for the world’s leading enterprise brands.

We invest in our people: We offer a comprehensive suite of benefits designed to help each member of our team thrive. Sprinklr believes that you should be able to get the type of care you need for your personal well-being when you need it. We offer you and your family voluntary healthcare coverage in countries where applicable. We believe it is important to take time off – it is essential for your mental and physical wellbeing. We provide Sprinklrites with paid time off to recharge and spend time with loved ones. We want to grow our talent with purpose. Our open Mentoring Program is designed to create meaningful connections that support growth and amplify our focus.

To learn more about employee benefits by region, click here.

To learn more about all-things-Sprinklr, visit our candidate resource hub here.

EEO - Our philosophy: Our goal is to ensure every employee feels like they belong and are operating in a collaborative environment. We fervently believe every employee matters and should be respected and heard. We believe we are stronger when we belong because collectively, we’re more innovative, creative, and successful.

Sprinklr is proud to be an equal-opportunity workplace and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, religion, creed, national origin or ancestry, ethnicity, sex (including gender, pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), age, physical or mental disability, citizenship, past, current, or prospective service in the uniformed services, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law.

Reasonable accommodations are available upon request during the interview process. To request an accommodation, please work directly with your recruitment coordinator or recruiter.

Warning about Recruiting Scams: Please be vigilant for recruiting scams impersonating Sprinklr. Sprinklr will never ask you for money, to pay for equipment, or for unnecessary personal information during the interview process. Sprinklr will also never pay in Bitcoin or send email communications from our executives. Please review the Federal Trade Commission's advice to avoid these types of scams.

title: Continuous Improvement Lead
description:
Continuous Improvement Lead

Department: Member Services
Location: London (Hybrid – minimum 3 days in office)
Contract: Permanent, full time

About the Team

PPL’s Member Services team is the primary point of contact for our members, delivering a proactive, high-quality service that supports them at every stage of their journey with PPL. The team actively recruits new members, represents PPL at industry events, and responds to member enquiries, ensuring accounts are accurate and up to date so members can confidently receive the royalties they are entitled to when their music is played. Our team is passionate about music and committed to providing an excellent experience for performers and recording rightsholders alike, helping to ensure they receive the rewards they deserve for their talent and investment.

What you’ll be doing:

As Continuous Improvement Lead, you’ll help shape and deliver practical improvements across Member Services, making it easier for colleagues to work efficiently and for members to receive a clear, accurate and high-quality service. This is a cross-functional role where you’ll use operational insight, data and stakeholder feedback to identify opportunities, prioritise improvements and turn ideas into embedded change.

You’ll manage the improvement pipeline from discovery through to delivery, working closely with colleagues across Member Services and wider PPL teams to scope requirements, agree solutions and support adoption. You’ll also play an important role in ensuring Member Services requirements are understood within Salesforce, ADP, automation and AI initiatives, helping to improve service quality, reduce risk and create measurable value for members, colleagues and the wider business.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead the Member Services continuous improvement agenda, ensuring opportunities are prioritised, shaped and delivered in line with operational priorities, member needs and business objectives.

  • Manage the improvement pipeline from idea through to implementation, translating operational insight, data and stakeholder feedback into clear scopes, business cases and delivery plans.

  • Deliver practical process, system and service improvements that increase efficiency, reduce risk, improve quality and strengthen the experience for members and colleagues.

  • Advise on Member Services requirements within Salesforce, ADP, automation and AI initiatives, ensuring operational needs are understood, tested and embedded effectively.

  • Oversee governance for key Member Services processes, guidance, forms and knowledge content, supporting clear ownership, version control, review cycles and consistent application.

  • Develop data-led insights and success measures that demonstrate the impact of improvements on service quality, efficiency, risk reduction, rework and the member experience.

  • Manage cross-functional engagement, workshops and feedback activity to align stakeholders, agree practical solutions and support effective adoption of change.

  • Deliver clear updates, recommendations and decision papers that support informed decision-making by senior leaders, governance forums and relevant boards.

About You

We’re looking for someone who is curious, organised and solutions-focused, with experience of delivering continuous improvement, operational change or process improvement activity. You’ll be confident using insight and evidence to identify opportunities, shape recommendations and influence decisions, while bringing people with you through clear communication and practical delivery.

You’ll enjoy working collaboratively across teams, facilitating conversations, testing assumptions and embedding improvements that make a real difference to how colleagues work, day to day. You’ll also be comfortable supporting, coaching or developing others, with direct responsibility for the Continuous Improvement Co-ordinator.

Key Requirements:

  • At least three years’ experience delivering continuous improvement, project management, operational change or process improvement activity.

  • Experience managing improvement work from discovery and requirements gathering through to implementation and adoption.

  • Strong planning, organisation and governance skills, with the ability to manage priorities, risks and dependencies.

  • Confident using data, feedback and process insight to identify issues, shape recommendations and evidence change.

  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence, facilitate and align operational, technical and specialist colleagues.

  • Comfortable working with business systems, reporting tools, process governance, data quality and controls.

  • PRINCE2 qualification or practical experience working with Agile/Scrum methodologies.

  • People management experience, including supporting, coaching or developing direct reports.

  • Experience with Salesforce, Microsoft 365, AI, automation or product roadmaps would be beneficial.

Why work at PPL?

When you join us at PPL, you’ll become part of a community united by a love for music and a mission to make a difference by championing music rights. Some key perks include:

  • Hybrid working and flexible working hours.

  • Work from anywhere in the world for up to 2 weeks per year.

  • Early finishes on Fridays in the summer months.

  • Private medical insurance, life assurance and health cash plan.

  • Annual allowance to claim back funds spent on your favourite music activity.

  • Free healthy breakfasts and fresh fruit every day.

  • Exclusive retail and gym discounts to support your wellbeing.

  • Season ticket loans.

  • Regular socials and music industry related events.

  • Annual bonus, which is non-contractual.

Equity, Diversity and Inclusion at PPL:

At PPL, we believe in fairness and in creating a work environment that respects all lived experiences. We are proud to represent musicians and performers from every section of society and are committed to cultivating a workplace where everyone feels welcome, and happy in a safe and trusted space.

description:
Job description:

Acknowledgement of Country

CSIRO acknowledges the Traditional Owners of the land, sea and waters, of the area that we live and work on across Australia. We acknowledge their continuing connection to their culture and pay our respects to their Elders past and present. View our vision towards reconciliation.

About CSIRO

As Australia's national science agency, CSIRO is solving the greatest challenges through innovative science and technology. Many of our iconic innovations were once considered impossible until someone, just like you, joined us and took on the challenge.

Visit CSIRO.au for more information.

The opportunity

As the Endpoint Platform Engineer within CSIRO's Information Management & Technology (IM&T) team, you will play a key role in supporting and enhancing the endpoint platforms that underpin Australia's national science agency.

Working across Windows, macOS and iOS environments, you'll help design, deploy, manage and improve secure, modern endpoint solutions using technologies such as Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Configuration Manager, JAMF Pro, Entra ID and Windows Autopilot.

Collaborating with a geographically dispersed team, you'll contribute to the delivery of enterprise endpoint services, application packaging, device management, security compliance, patching and automation initiatives, ensuring staff across CSIRO's scientific, corporate and operational environments have reliable, secure and high-performing technology solutions.

High-level duties include:

  • Administer, support and improve CSIRO's managed endpoint services across Windows, macOS and iOS using Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Configuration Manager, Group Policy, JAMF Pro, Apple Business Manager and related enterprise endpoint management technologies.
  • Configure and maintain endpoint enrolment, provisioning and management workflows, including Windows Autopilot, Microsoft Intune enrolment, Microsoft Configuration Manager, Apple Automated Device Enrolment, mobile device management workflows, configuration profiles and Volume Purchase Program application management.
  • Package, test, deploy and maintain applications, scripts, configuration changes and self-service workflows for managed Windows and macOS endpoints.
  • Support endpoint operating system lifecycle activities across Windows, macOS and iOS, including upgrades, patching, compliance reporting, troubleshooting, remediation and end-user support escalation.
  • Administer and support Windows endpoint engineering activities, including Microsoft Configuration Manager, Microsoft Intune, Windows Autopilot, Windows Update for Business, Group Policy, application deployment, endpoint configuration and compliance remediation.
  • Administer and support Apple endpoint engineering activities, including macOS and iOS devices managed through JAMF Pro, Apple Business Manager, Automated Device Enrolment, Volume Purchase Program, Microsoft Intune, configuration profiles, application deployment and compliance remediation.

Role particulars

Location and office arrangements: Kensington WA, clayton VIC, Black Mountain ACT, Waite SA, St Lucia QLD

Salary: AU$100,103 - AU$113,251 per annum (pro rata for part-time), plus 15.4% superannuation

Tenure & work schedule: Indefinite

Reference: 103600

As the successful candidate, you will bring:

Essential criteria

title: Jr. Software Engineer
description:
Job Summary:

Silvervine Software builds and supports the insurance systems that carriers and their partners rely on every day — policy administration, claims, rating and payments. We are hiring a junior software engineer to join our LAAIR team.

The team owns SvApi, the Silvervine API layer that connects our insurance platform to the outside systems it depends on. When an agent asks for a home or auto quote, SvApi is what reaches out to the data vendors, pulls back motor vehicle records, prior loss history, property valuations and credit information, and turns all of it into a rate. Most of our work is integration work: talking to third-party APIs that we do not control, mapping their responses into our own models, and working out what went wrong when a vendor changes something without telling us.

This is a genuine junior role, not a senior role with a junior title. You will start on well-scoped pieces of that work in C# and ASP.NET Core, with a senior developer reviewing everything you write, and your scope will grow as you learn the domain. We expect you to be new at this. We do not expect you to already know insurance. What we are looking for is solid fundamentals in C# and SQL, care when reading a specification, and the willingness to say early when something does not make sense.

Please read the full job description before applying. It contains specific instructions on what to include in your application, and we do read for them.

Job Description:

About the role

You will join the LAAIR team, which owns SvApi — the Silvervine API layer that sits between our insurance platform and the many outside systems it depends on. When an agent asks for a home or auto quote, SvApi is what goes out to the data vendors, pulls back motor-vehicle records, prior loss history, property valuations and credit scores, and turns all of it into a rate.

That means most of our work is integration work: talking to third-party APIs that we do not control, mapping their responses into our models, and figuring out what went wrong when a vendor changes something without telling us.

You will start on well-scoped pieces of this, with a senior developer reviewing everything you write. As you learn the domain, the scope grows. We expect you to be new at this. We do not expect you to already know insurance.

What you'll work on

  • Building and maintaining REST endpoints in C# and ASP.NET Core across our service set — rating, policy, claims, motor-vehicle records, VIN lookup, loss history, flood risk and document generation.
  • Integrating third-party insurance data providers. Reading a vendor's schema or documentation, modelling their response, and mapping it into ours. Some of them use clean JSON; some hand you an XML schema that rejects your request for reasons it declines to explain.
  • Response mapping and projections — deciding which fields our API surfaces to a partner, and making sure none of them silently go missing.
  • Writing unit and integration tests for your own work, before it is reviewed. We have a standing test-coverage backlog and you will spend real time in it — it is one of the fastest ways to learn a codebase you did not write.
  • Applying cross-cutting concerns service by service — request validation, global exception handling, security headers, caching. Repetitive by nature, but it takes you through every service we own.
  • Moving duplicated code into shared libraries. We are consolidating common serialization and filtering into a core package, one service at a time.
  • Debugging production integration failures. A partner reports a 400 that should have been a 401; a response is dropping a field; a cached token is expiring wrong. You will read logs, compare against the legacy platform's behavior, and find it.
  • Sprint ceremonies: planning, refinement, standup and retrospective.

What we need from you

  • Working knowledge of C# and the .NET ecosystem (.NET 6 or newer).
  • Comfort with REST APIs — you have called one, and ideally built one.
  • Enough JSON and/or XML serialization experience to know that mapping between two models is where the bugs live.
  • Enough SQL to write a join, a GROUP BY, and reason about why a query returns the wrong row count.
  • Familiarity with git and pull-request workflow.
  • The ability to say “I don't understand this yet” early rather than late. On a team whose job is integrating systems nobody fully documents, this matters more to us than raw speed.
  • Zero to three years of professional experience, a relevant degree, or a portfolio that shows the same.

Nice to have

None of these are required. They reflect what is actually in our stack.

  • ASP.NET Core Reflex Endpoints experience
  • Azure — App Service, SQL Database, Service Bus, Application Insights, DevOps pipelines
  • Entity Framework Core or Dapper
  • xUnit, NUnit or MSTest — any test framework you have actually written tests in
  • FluentValidation, or any request-validation library
  • OpenAPI / Swagger — writing or consuming an API contract
  • Infrastructure as code (Bicep, Terraform, ARM)
  • Any prior contact with insurance, financial or other regulated-industry software
  • Any exposure to legacy CFML / ColdFusion — parts of the platform we integrate with are written in it, and knowing that going in is a genuine plus

Not every bullet in this section will be familiar to a junior developer, and that is fine — it is a wish list, not a checklist. If a bullet here means nothing to you, say so in your application. “I had to look that up and could not find it” is a completely acceptable answer, and it will not count against you. Claiming experience you do not have will.

How to apply

Your application includes three short questions. Please answer all three — we read them, and they carry real weight in how we shortlist.

  • Which item under “What you'll work on” do you feel least prepared for, and what would you do about it in your first month? One or two sentences. We are looking for an honest read on yourself, not reassurance.
  • Is there anything in the “Nice to have” list you are unfamiliar with? Naming it will not count against you.
  • Share a small piece of code you wrote yourself — a repository link, or fifteen lines pasted in — and one sentence on what you would change about it today.

A note on AI assistance

We use AI tools at Silvervine and we expect you to use them too. Using an assistant to help write your application is fine. Sending us something you have not read is not.

So, plainly: if you use an AI assistant on this application, read what it produced before you send it. Everything you submit is yours to stand behind in the interview, and we will ask you about it.

title: Data Governance Consultant (IDMC / CDGC)
description:
Why Keyrus, Why Now!

Keyrus is an international group of 2,800 consultants and experts across 28 countries, built on a single conviction: AI does not transform businesses. Architected intelligence does.

For more than 30 years, we have been building the data foundations that make intelligent systems work — designing the Operating System of the intelligent enterprise, where intelligence is embedded into the core of business processes to create sustainable value: we operationalise intelligence.

AI does not replace humans. It repositions us to a place no system can follow: understanding, deciding, designing, and creating.

At Keyrus, you will not just develop skills — you will develop judgment. Your expertise sharpens with every system you architect, every client challenge you solve, and every deployment that compounds on the last.

Over time, you grow into one of the rarest professionals of the intelligence era: someone who bridges data, AI, and human decision-making at scale, across industries and geographies. This is not a role you fill. It is a discipline you master and a story you help write to become a Keyrus Architect of Intelligence.

Technology amplifies. Keyrus culture differentiates. Industrial discipline connects the two.

Role Details

📍 Job location: Portugal or Spain (Remote)
🕒 Contract type: Contractor B2B / 4-month project
🗓 Target start date: ASAP
⏰ Working hours: Full-time

📋 What You'll Architect

As a Data Governance Platform Implementation Consultant, you will help organisations transform complexity into measurable outcomes by combining technology, data, intelligence, and human decision-making.

This role is both technical and consultative - perfect for someone who can combine hands-on development, solution design, and leadership of client delivery. We’re looking for professionals who think like architects and act like builders.

You will lead the implementation of Informatica Intelligent Data Management Cloud (IDMC), with a focus on Cloud Data Governance and Catalog (CDGC), delivering an MVP that will serve as the blueprint for future deployments in multiple countries.

Working closely with central data teams, regional stakeholders, and data governance leaders, you will play a key role in defining how the platform should be configured, activated, and scaled, balancing business value, governance objectives, and operational costs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Implement and configure Informatica IDMC / CDGC, establishing the foundation for a global data governance platform

  • Configure connectors, source system integrations, scanning and profiling capabilities across the organisation

  • Define and recommend platform activation priorities, advising stakeholders on the most effective implementation approach

  • Assess and communicate the cost implications of configuration choices and regional requirements

  • Collaborate with international stakeholders, including central data teams, US-based governance teams, and regional business units

  • Act as a trusted advisor, providing technical guidance, implementation recommendations, and governance best practices.

👤 Who You Are

  • You are curious, analytical, and motivated by solving meaningful business challenges

  • You enjoy turning complexity into clarity and action

  • You balance technical expertise with strategic thinking and business understanding

  • You are comfortable influencing stakeholders and making recommendations in ambiguous environments

  • You take ownership of your work and can independently drive key implementation decisions.

  • You thrive in multicultural and international environments

  • You are interested in emerging technologies, innovation, and the potential of GenAI-driven optimisation within data management and governance

  • You communicate clearly and confidently with both technical and non-technical audiences.

🛠️ What You Bring

Qualifications & Experience

  • 7+ years of experience in Data Governance, Metadata Management, Data Management, or related disciplines

  • Strong hands-on experience implementing Informatica Intelligent Data Management Cloud (IDMC) solutions and Cloud Data Governance and Catalog (CDGC)

  • Proven experience delivering end-to-end enterprise-scale data governance, metadata management, or data catalog initiatives and implementation

  • Experience working within multinational, federated, or multi-entity environments

  • Professional fluency in English.

Technical & Professional Skills

  • Strong expertise in Informatica IDMC, including platform configuration and deployment

  • Experience configuring connectors, source onboarding, scanning, profiling, and metadata discovery processes

  • Ability to define implementation priorities and make architecture-level recommendations

  • Understanding of data governance operating models, data ownership, stewardship, and domain-based approaches

  • Ability to evaluate and articulate the operational and financial impact of technical decisions

  • Strong stakeholder management and consulting skills

  • Experience working with APIs, integrations, and enterprise data platform ecosystems

  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving capabilities.

Nice to Have

  • Experience defining data governance frameworks, standards, and guidelines

  • Previous experience in the insurance, financial services, or assistance services sectors

  • Exposure to large-scale international transformation programmes

  • Experience working alongside Informatica Professional Services teams

  • Knowledge of emerging trends in Data Management, Data Governance, AI, and GenAI-enabled optimisation

  • Relevant Informatica certifications.

⭐ What Makes You Successful

  • You focus on outcomes rather than activity.

  • You approach challenges with curiosity and pragmatism.

  • You communicate complex concepts in a clear and accessible way.

  • You are comfortable navigating ambiguity and finding practical solutions.

  • You contribute to collective intelligence by sharing knowledge and supporting others.

  • You combine autonomy with collaboration.

  • You continuously look for opportunities to improve systems, processes, and results.

🎁 What We Offer at Keyrus Portugal

  • Competitive salary aligned with your experience and the data market

  • Meal allowance: €10.20/day

  • Flexible benefits plan

  • Private medical insurance

  • 22 days of annual leave, increasing every 3 years (up to 25 days)

  • Continuous learning via KLX – Keyrus Learning Experience

  • A collaborative, international, and human-centred work environment

💰 How Our Salary Ranges Work

At Keyrus, salary ranges reflect different levels of mastery and impact within the same role — not different job titles.

  • Bottom of the range
    You meet the core requirements and will need ramp-up time and support.

  • Middle of the range
    You are fully autonomous from Day 1 and deliver consistently.

  • Top of the range
    You are a reference for the role, mentor others, and raise the bar for the team.

Final offers are based on experience, autonomy, scope, and market context, and are discussed transparently during the process.

🔒 Responsible AI & Recruitment

At Keyrus, all stages of our recruitment process are conducted and evaluated by human recruiters and interviewers.
To support accuracy and efficiency, AI may occasionally be used internally by our team exclusively for note-taking purposes during interviews. AI is never used to make decisions.

To ensure fairness, authenticity, and the protection of confidential and proprietary information, the use of AI tools by candidates during the recruitment process is strictly prohibited.

Our commitment to responsible AI practices ensures that hiring decisions are based solely on each candidate’s own skills, experience, judgment, and expertise.

⚠️ Any use of AI assistance during the interview process may result in immediate disqualification from the recruitment process.

♿ Equal Opportunity Statement

We are committed to building an inclusive workplace and encourage applications from all backgrounds, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic.

description:
We Are Inspired to Serve. Join us!

The Certified Medication Assistant (CMA) / Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) is responsible for providing high-quality resident
care in alignment with the organization’s mission, values, and regulatory requirements. This dual-certified role ensures the safe
and accurate assistance of medications under the direction of a nurse, while also providing direct, hands-on support with
activities of daily living to promote dignity, independence, and overall well-being. The CMA/CNA collaborates closely with nursing
and caregiving teams to support a person-centered care environment and ensure residents attain or maintain the highest possible physical, mental, and emotional health. This role functions as both a Certified Nursing Assistant and a Certified Medication Aide in accordance with applicable state regulations.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Under the supervision of the Nurse, assists with medication and provides treatments according to physician’s orders and in accordance with facility policy. Provides, completes and documents assigned timely and accurately.
  • Maintain resident rooms in a clean and orderly manner by providing light housekeeping, changing linen, making beds, putting away clothing and personal effects, tidying bedside table, shelves, closets, and cleaning bathrooms, etc.
  • Provide direct care and assistance with activities of daily living including bathing, dressing, toileting, grooming, mobility, and feeding.
  • Position is service in nature; in performance of duties the resident care assistant is entrusted to assist residents with basic personal care according to procedures and daily assignment. This includes but is not limited to bathing, dressing, dental hygiene, toilet activities, grooming, feeding, transportation/transfer,etc. The role assist residents with transfers, ambulation, and supportive devices using proper safety techniques.
  • Attends and participates in facility meetings and in-service training programs.
  • Practices good infection control techniques in all aspects of resident care. Prepare residents for meals, assist with serving meals and feeding of residents.
  • Observes residents’ rights including, but not limited to, privacy, dignity, etc.
  • Observe residents and promptly report changes in condition, behavior, or functional status. Safeguards the resident’s privacy and property.
  • Participates in the orientation of new or temporary staff to the unit to assure continuity in the delivery of resident care.
  • Promotes positive public relations with residents, family members and guests.
  • Provides restorative care to residents as assigned by the Nurse or as indicated in the overall plan of care.
  • Assists with admissions, discharges, and transfers
  • Must be able to give clear and concise direction to staff and others.

EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE:

  • Required Degree: High School Diploma or Equivalent
  • Preferred Degree: N/A
  • Preferred Certificate(s): Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA), Certified Medication Aide (CMA) and CPR. In accordance with State regulations to ensure proper training, certifications or licensure.
  • Experience: 0-1 Years

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITY:

  • Ability to communicate effectively with residents and healthcare professionals.
  • Knowledge of various medications, their purposes, dosages, routes of administration, and potential side effects.
  • Knowledge of privacy regulations and maintaining patient confidentiality.
  • Knowledge of record-keeping skills to document medication administration and patient responses accurately.
  • Ability to educate patients about their medications.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

title: Chief Information Security Officer (Charlotte)
description:
WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Reporting to the SVP & Chief Information Officer, James Olender, the CISO must be able to:

  • Mitigate Third-Party & Supply Chain Risk: Develop robust protocols to manage the cybersecurity of a global, interconnected supply chain, ensuring that ADI's digital products and services remain resilient against sophisticated hybrid attacks.
  • Translate Risk into Financial Terms: Quantify and communicate cyber risks as financial and operational impact to the Board and the Audit and Compliance Committee, ensuring security investments are aligned with ADI's Long Term revenue goals and sustainability mission.
  • Lead a \Shared Responsibility\ Culture: Evangelize a culture of cyber awareness across ADI's 5,000+ employees and global partner network, moving security from a technical hurdle to a proactive business enabler that builds customer trust.
  • Standardize Global Governance: Drive the adoption of consistent global standards (such as NIST and ISO 27001) across ADI's global locations to ensure a baseline of \cyber hygiene\ that supports ADI’s ongoing digital expansion.
HOW YOU WILL DO IT:
  • Develop and implement a strategic, long-term security strategy that protects ADI's global information assets.
  • Work with senior business leaders to assess and communicate acceptable levels of risk across diverse global markets and critical infrastructure projects.
  • Identify and report on security risks to the Executive team and the Audit and Compliance Committee of the Board, providing expertise on industrial and data standards.
  • Deliver Board updates, presenting ADI's security posture directly and in alignment with Board expectations.
  • Manage a high‑visibility Board environment where cyber risks must be escalated rapidly and communicated with clarity, precision, and real‑time responsiveness.
  • Develop, mentor, and manage a high-performing global team of security professionals, fostering expertise in Cloud Security, Application Security, and Product Security.
  • Identify, establish, and continuously enhance cybersecurity policies, standards, and tooling embedded within ADI’s enterprise AI strategy, ensuring responsible, secure adoption of AI across products, platforms, and operations.
  • Ensure cyber resilience of critical distribution operations, including order fulfillment, warehouse execution, transportation systems, store fronts, and customer service platforms.
  • Implement necessary controls to secure and protect branch operations, point-of-sale systems, customer-facing technologies, and distributed edge computing environments.
  • Protect customer-facing ecommerce platforms from fraud, account takeover, bot attacks, payment fraud, and digital commerce disruption.
  • Leverage AI‑driven security capabilities to strengthen threat detection and response, enabling proactive defense against emerging cyber risks and accelerating ADI's ability to anticipate, prevent, and mitigate sophisticated attacks.
  • Ensure the security program complies with international data privacy laws (e.g., GDPR) and emerging cybersecurity regulations.
  • Act as the primary champion for a \Security‑by‑Design\ culture, ensuring that security is a competitive advantage for ADI's digital solutions.
  • Partner with Enterprise Architects and Product Engineering teams to ensure ADI's platforms are developed according to secure coding and infrastructure guidelines.
  • Manage global intrusion detection and vulnerability reporting, coordinating with Internal Audit and external partners to remediate risks across all technology environments.
  • Develop KPI metrics that measure the effectiveness of the security program and demonstrate continuous maturity in alignment with the NIST framework.
  • Monitor the global threat landscape for emerging risks, advising stakeholders on proactive defense measures.
  • Own enterprise cyber resilience strategy including operational recovery, business continuity planning, cyber crisis management, and executive tabletop exercises.
  • Oversee incident response planning and breach investigations, coordinating with Legal and Communications to manage impacts on customers and public trust.
  • Lead the creation of a comprehensive Supply Chain Risk Management process to secure ADI's vendor ecosystem and digital partners.
  • Lead cybersecurity due diligence and rapid post‑acquisition integration for M&A activity.
  • Support public company governance requirements, cybersecurity disclosures, SEC reporting obligations, and Audit Committee oversight processes.
WHAT YOU MUST HAVE:
  • Minimum 10–15 years of IT and/or business leadership experience, with at least 7 years specifically in senior information security/cybersecurity roles within a multinational organization.
  • A proven track record in developing global security strategies that encompass both Enterprise IT and Product security roadmaps.
  • Extensive knowledge of business risk and the ability to conduct real‑time risk assessments for enterprise and product services.
  • Exceptional ability to translate complex cyber threats into business and sustainability impacts for Executive Management and the Audit and Compliance Committee.
  • Experience presenting cybersecurity strategy, incident response, and risk posture directly to public company Boards and Audit Committees.
  • Experience managing compliance with global privacy, cybersecurity, and digital operational resilience regulations.
WHAT WE WOULD VALUE:
  • A natural coalition builder with the ability to inspire interdisciplinary teams to achieve unified global security goals.
  • Experienced in negotiating complex SaaS, Cloud, and Managed Security Services (MSS) contracts with global vendors.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead incident response and disaster recovery in high‑pressure situations, particularly those involving critical infrastructure.
  • A leader of leaders who embodies the highest level of values and ethics
  • Prior experience in distribution, logistics, ecommerce, retail, manufacturing, or similarly complex operational environments preferred.

title: Combustion and Emissions Systems Engineer
description:
We are looking for a talented Combustion and Emissions Systems Engineer to join our Cummins Inc. team onsite in Seymour, Indiana.

In this role, you will make an impact in the following ways:

  • Investigate thermal and fluid system challenges to identify root causes and deliver data-driven solutions that improve product performance.
  • Apply combustion, emissions, thermodynamics, heat transfer, and fluid dynamics principles to support innovative and environmentally responsible product development.
  • Leverage analytical, simulation, and experimental methods to influence design decisions and optimize system architectures.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams to drive informed technical decisions and project success.
  • Execute validation, testing, and verification activities that improve product reliability, quality, and customer satisfaction.
  • Support the development and advancement of engineering processes, tools, and best practices that enhance technical excellence.
  • Analyze technical data and performance trends to mitigate risks, solve complex problems, and improve product capability.
  • Contribute to the successful delivery of new technologies and product enhancements throughout the product development lifecycle.

To be successful in this role, you will need the following:

  • Foundational knowledge of thermal and fluid sciences, including combustion, emissions, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and energy conversion systems.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to interpret data, evaluate system performance, and make sound engineering recommendations.
  • Ability to apply systems thinking and engineering methodologies to translate stakeholder needs into effective technical solutions.
  • Effective collaboration and communication skills with the ability to work across technical disciplines and contribute to shared project objectives.
  • Growth mindset with a commitment to continuous learning, technical development, and delivering results in a dynamic engineering environment.

Education, Licenses, Certifications:

  • College, university, or equivalent Bachelor's degree in Engineering or appropriate STEM field is required.
  • Post-graduate (Master's) degree relevant to this discipline area may be required for select roles.
  • This position may require licensing for compliance with export controls or sanctions regulations.

Expectations:

  • Entry level/Early career professional.
  • Preferred candidates would have relevant experience working in either a temporary student employment environment (intern, co-op, or other extracurricular team activities) or as an early career professional in a relevant technical discipline area.
  • Knowledge of MS Office tools is also preferred.

Additional Responsibilities & Preferred Key Competencies:

  • Support engine emissions audit testing activities, including test execution, data collection, analysis, and compliance reporting.
  • Investigate engine performance concerns at the Seymour Engine Plant and provide technical recommendations that improve product quality and operational performance.
  • Utilize engineering tools, technologies, and emissions data systems to support engineering analysis and decision-making.
  • Apply statistical analysis, modeling, simulation, and validation techniques to evaluate system behavior and support product development initiatives.
  • Contribute to Product Problem Solving (PPS), Value Package Change (VPC), Engineering Standard Work (ESW), and Functional Excellence Practices (FEP) activities.
  • Support product verification and validation plans through analytical, simulation, and physical testing methods that ensure product capability and performance.
  • Demonstrate strong technical documentation skills by clearly communicating findings, recommendations, and engineering decisions to stakeholders.
  • Thrive in a collaborative environment by exhibiting adaptability, sound judgment, initiative, and a customer-focused approach to solving technical challenges.
  • Preferred experience with engine testing, product performance evaluation, data acquisition systems, test cell operations, and engine emissions regulations.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Teams, Outlook) and MATLAB for data analysis, modeling, simulation, reporting, and technical problem solving.

What you'll be doing

  • Lead the day-to-day performance of your team, monitoring individual and team KPIs including service levels, first case resolution, handling times, adherence and quality.

  • Coach, mentor and develop Customer Experience Consultants through regular feedback, quality assessments and performance reviews.

  • Ensure guests receive a high-quality, professional experience across phone, email and webchat.

  • Manage team performance, absence and attrition effectively while recognising and celebrating great performance.

  • Analyse trends in customer enquiries and performance data to identify opportunities to improve workflows, efficiency and service.

  • Oversee daily operations to ensure response and resolution SLAs are achieved.

  • Act as the first escalation point for complex customer issues, supporting effective and timely resolutions.

  • Collaborate with the Contact Centre Manager, Resource Planning, Trainers and other teams to maximise productivity and continuously improve the guest experience.

  • Build engagement through regular huddles, feedback, recognition, incentives and team activities.

  • Help embed consistent ways of working across teams and locations, sharing knowledge and best practice.

Who we’re looking for

You’ll thrive in this role if you enjoy bringing out the best in people, solving problems and using data to turn insights into action. You’re comfortable in a fast-paced environment, can adapt quickly when priorities change and know how to balance a great guest experience with strong operational performance.

We’re looking for someone who brings:

  • Proven experience supervising or leading day-to-day contact centre operations.

  • A strong understanding of contact centre processes, performance management and service delivery.

  • Great people management skills, with the ability to coach, mentor, motivate and develop others.

  • Confidence handling complaints, escalations and difficult conversations.

  • Strong communication and active listening skills, including the ability to recognise different customer needs and de-escalate challenging situations.

  • A hands-on, structured and proactive approach to problem solving.

  • The ability to work effectively in a dynamic and changing environment.

  • A collaborative mindset and the ability to build strong relationships across teams.

How you'll make an impact

  • Lead an engaged, motivated and high-performing team that consistently delivers for our guests.

  • Improve guest experiences by coaching for quality, effective communication and first-time resolution.

  • Use performance data to proactively manage service levels, handling times, adherence, quality and productivity.

  • Identify recurring issues and turn them into coaching opportunities, process improvements or longer-term solutions.

  • Champion consistent standards and ways of working across teams and locations.

  • Create clarity for your team, set expectations and make informed decisions that deliver positive outcomes for both people and performance.

Why you’ll want to work at Awaze

We offer a versatile position in a strong professional and social environment - one you’ll have the opportunity to influence and help shape. You’ll be part of an international company that invests in the future, and join a dynamic, fast-paced department with skilled and committed colleagues who support each other.

We’re a people-first business - and we know that our success starts with our teams. Here’s a glimpse of what you’ll enjoy:

  • Generous discounts on holidays across our brands

  • Real opportunities to grow, learn and shape your role as well as careers progression vertically or horizontally, cross countries and responsibilities.

About Awaze

At Awaze, we bring holidays to life. With over 110,000 holiday homes across 25 countries, we’re Europe’s largest holiday rentals company. Our purpose is simple – to delight our guests and homeowners while building an inspiring place to work for our people.

Awaze A/S is part of Europe’s leading provider of holiday homes. The company operates more than 25 historical brands, including , NOVASOL, and Hoseasons.

You will be employed by Awaze A/S and work with the NOVASOL brand, which has the largest selection of holiday homes in Denmark and over 50,000 holiday homes across Europe.

Worth knowing

This position is full-time (40 hours), temporary (12 months) and fully office-based in Lowestoft. Our Contact Centres open Monday-Sunday 9am-8pm, so full flexibility is essential for success in this role.

What’s next?

If this sounds like the right next step for you, hit “Apply” and follow the instructions to submit your application. We tailor our recruitment process to each role to give both you and our hiring teams the best possible chance to assess whether this could be the start of a successful collaboration. You’ll hear from us shortly after we’ve reviewed your application.

We’re committed to running an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. All applicants will receive equal consideration for employment, and if you have any specific requirements or adjustments needed for the interview, just let us know when you accept your invitation - we’re happy to accommodate.

title: Retail Merchandise Mgr
description:

title: Lifeguard - Pearl British Academy - AY 2026/2027
description:
Aldar Academies are currently seeking a Lifeguard for the Pearl British Academy, commencing August 2026.

Successful candidates will find themselves welcomed into a wonderful school family community, where staff are held in high regard by pupil, parents and school leadership alike.

Main Duties

  • Ensuring the children are supervised at all times.

  • Support the coach and PE team in planning and delivering engaging lessons.

  • Support in organising and participating in galas and other sports related activities.

  • Supporting class teachers and classroom assistants over the care and supervision of children- prior to, during and after lessons.

  • Supporting PE team in running extra-curricular provisions.

Specific Duties:

Teaching and Learning:

  • Maintain full supervision of the swimming pool and its users from the designated station.

  • Ensuring pool checks are completed and recorded before and after the lessons, where applicable, and liaising with maintenance teams where corrective action needs to be made.

  • Managing and ensuring the safety of swimmers, parents, pupils, teachers, staff and any other persons on site.

  • To support teachers and Swimming Coach with administrative tasks and offering excellent customer service support at all times.

  • To read, understand and work within the Normal Operating Procedure and Emergency Action Plan (PSOP-Pool Safety Operating Procedure) that is supplied by the school in line with ADEK’s guidelines.

  • To work within the Health & Safety, Control of Substances Hazardous to Health (COSHH) and Risk Assessment guidelines that is supplied by the school.

  • To carry out safety/operational equipment and resource checks where requested and report findings in appropriate documentation. All documentation is to be supplied by the school.

  • To manoeuvre, set-up and dismantle equipment in a safe and efficient manner in accordance with an induction that is provided by the school.

  • To help maintain a safe and secure environment through observation and provision of guidance and emergency assistance when required.

  • To report any concerns about any areas of operation to the relevant line manager or Swimming Instructor.

  • Attending mandatory monthly training sessions to maintain knowledge, fitness and skills required to carry out your duties.

  • To carry out pool tests as per the PSOP, in accordance with training and induction.

  • To represent Aldar Education in a professional and positive manner at all times, adhering to company values.

  • To support the PE department with day to day tasks and whole school events when not required at poolside.

Behaviour management and duties:

  • Follow the school’s established policies and procedures, e.g., behavior, NSOPs, code of conduct and child safeguarding policy.

  • Manage classes effectively, using approaches which are appropriate to students’ needs in order to inspire, motivate and challenge pupils.

  • Maintain good relationships with pupils, exercise appropriate authority, and act decisively when necessary, within the school’s established policies.

  • Be a positive role model and demonstrate consistently the positive attitudes, values, and behaviour, which are expected of pupils.

  • Have high expectations of good conduct, promoting self-control and independence of all learners.

  • To ensure a safe and secure environment that allows for appropriate social, emotional, and academic growth for all students.

  • Carry out duties as directed and within the school’s established policies.

Wider professional responsibilities:

  • To work as part of a curriculum action group, supporting planning, assessment, resources, and special events linked to the team.

  • Support in organizing and taking part in school events, outings and extra-curricular activities (ECAs) which may take place at weekends or after school hours.

  • Make a positive contribution to the wider life and ethos of the school.

  • Take initiative of own professional development to secure high quality teaching and for successful execution of roles and responsibilities.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • UAE approved (ADQCC) Swimming Coach or pool Lifeguard Certificate.
  • First Aid Certificate and CPR knowledge

Minimum Experience:

  • To be a competent instructor, able to support the needs of all learners.
  • To be qualified to teach swimming.
  • To be a qualified life guard.

Job Specific Knowledge & Skills:

  • Flexible in approach to work.
  • Must be a proficient swimmer.
  • CPR knowledge.
  • Actively involved in co-curricular activities.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English. Arabic proficiency desired.
  • Must be physically fit and able to work outdoors.
  • A high level of professionalism and consideration of the well-being of children.
  • Able to work as part of a team, sharing ideas, giving and receiving feedback.

Application:

A covering letter and CV including details of two referees should be sent via the careers page.

WHAT WE OFFER:

Aldar Education is a family of world-class, child centered, and innovative schools based in the UAE. We educate over 25,000 students across our group of owned and managed schools and as we grow so does our need for highly skilled, inspirational, and dedicated school leaders. Our future-focused learning model includes both students and staff and so we place a special emphasis on professional development, coaching and training.

Successful candidates will have access to a wide network of professionals and opportunities to both lead and contribute to training others as well as developing themselves.

Aspen Dental – Private Practice of Cherry Creek
Denver, CO – Cherry Creek

  • Consistent part-time schedule

  • Established private practice in Cherry Creek

Advanced Dentistry in a Private-Practice Setting

The practice is committed to remaining at the forefront of dental technology. Clinical resources include advanced laser dentistry, including Fotona technology, along with a comprehensive restorative and implant-focused environment.

For a Periodontist, that means working alongside doctors who understand complex treatment planning and value collaborative specialty care.

  • Comprehensive periodontal diagnosis and treatment planning

  • Surgical periodontal therapy

  • Soft-tissue procedures

  • Osseous surgery

  • Crown lengthening

  • Bone grafting

  • Implant-related periodontal care

  • Dental implant placement

  • Periodontal maintenance planning

  • Laser periodontal procedures

  • Collaborative treatment planning with restorative doctors

The practice already provides implant, restorative, cosmetic, and periodontal services, creating an environment where specialty treatment can integrate naturally into comprehensive patient care.

  • DDS or DMD from an accredited dental school

  • Completion of an accredited Periodontics residency program

  • Active Colorado dental license, or ability to obtain one

  • Board certification or board eligibility preferred

  • Strong periodontal surgical skills

  • Implant experience preferred

  • Excellent diagnostic and treatment-planning ability

  • Strong communication with patients and referring/restorative doctors

  • Commitment to a high level of clinical quality

  • Professional, collaborative, patient-centered approach

  • Experience with laser periodontal therapy is a plus.

Why Aspen Dental – Private Practice of Cherry Creek?

This is not a high-volume corporate specialty rotation. It is an established Cherry Creek private practice built around sophisticated dentistry, advanced technology, individualized treatment, and patient comfort.

You'll have the opportunity to work with an experienced dental team in a setting that values quality over shortcuts and supports comprehensive treatment planning across periodontal, implant, restorative, and cosmetic dentistry.

About the Practice

Aspen Dental – Private Practice of Cherry Creek is located at 3300 East 1st Avenue, Suite 300, Denver, CO 80206, in the heart of Cherry Creek.

The practice provides comprehensive dental care ranging from preventive and restorative dentistry to dental implants, cosmetic treatment, sedation dentistry, periodontal therapy, and advanced laser procedures.

Let's Talk

If you are a Periodontist looking for a consistent Monday schedule, $1,000–$2,000 daily compensation, advanced technology, and a high-quality private-practice environment, we would love to connect.

Apply today to learn more about joining Aspen Dental – Private Practice of Cherry Creek.

title: Quality Associate II - QMS
description:
SUMMARY OF POSITION:

The Quality Associate II – Quality Management System (QMS) supports the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the QMS in alignment with ISO 13485, ISO 9001, FDA QMSR, and, as applicable, pharmaceutical cGMP requirements (21 CFR Parts 210/211 and ICH Q7), among other applicable requirements. This role focuses on CAPA, Internal Audits, Supporting External Audits, Training, Batch Release, and Supplier Qualification and Quality Agreements, QMS-level risk management. The position ensures the QMS remains compliant, effective, and inspection-ready.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS, included but not limited to:

QMS Quality Oversight

  • Administer and maintain QMS processes including CAPA, internal audits and training SOPs.
  • Lead or support CAPA investigations, ensuring strong root-cause analysis, effectiveness checks, and timely closure.
  • Support internal audit planning, execution, reporting, and follow-up activities.
  • Support QA Manager and QMS Documentation Lead with document control and change management activities, including SOPs, forms, labels, IFUs, and controlled templates.
  • Maintain and oversee the training management system.
  • Support QA review of the feedback and complaint handling activities, escalate to Regulatory as needed.
  • Perform quality review of supplier approval process, including risk assessments.
  • Review and approve batch records and final product documentation.
  • Support risk management activities (ISO 14971), as needed.
  • Perform trend analysis across QMS processes (CAPA, complaints, audits, training, etc.) and escalate trends. Prepare reports for quality review board, management review, etc.
  • Support the training program by managing the training matrix, ensuring training assignments are accurate, current, and aligned with role requirements; monitor completion status and maintain compliant training records.

Batch Release

  • Review and approve batch records and final product documentation.
  • Ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance of DHRs, COAs, and supporting documentation.

Documentation & Compliance

  • Ensure quality related documentation complies with ISO 13485, ISO 9001 and FDA 21 CFR 820 (QMSR), and other applicable requirements.
  • Draft, revise, and maintain SOPs, work instructions, forms, and controlled documents as required.
  • Support and participate in internal and external audits.
  • Ensure that batch reviews are conducted by personnel independent from the manufacturing, production or testing activities to ensure objective assessment and prevent conflicts of interest.

Documentation & Compliance

  • Ensure quality related documentation complies with ISO 13485, ISO 9001 and FDA 21 CFR 820 (QMSR)
  • Support operations in ensuring their documentation complies with requirements as applicable, ISO 13485, ISO 9001 and FDA 21 CFR 820 (QMSR), etc.
  • Draft, revise, and maintain SOPs, work instructions, forms, and controlled documents related to operations quality.
  • Support internal and external audits by providing quality records and participating in audit activities.

Training & Cross-Functional Support

  • Provide training on QMS, Continuous Improvements GMP, GDP, and compliance requirements, as applicable.
  • Cross-train with the Quality team and provide support during peak workload periods.
  • Collaborate with Manufacturing, Procurement, Technical Support, Compliance (QC, RA) and other departments as applicable to ensure compliant operations.

OTHER FUNCTIONS:

  • Ensure compliance with safety regulations and procedures are implemented and followed; Maintain clean and safe work area.
