title: Escrow Insurance Servicing Technician II
description:
If you are motivated and believe in the credit union philosophy of "People Helping People," join our team!

Position Overview:

Oversees the end-to-end operational accuracy and regulatory compliance of mortgage escrow accounts across the organization’s real estate portfolio. Responsible for supervising the ongoing tracking, recalculation, and timely disbursement of property taxes, homeowners’ insurance, and flood coverage. Serves as the point of contact for escrow administration, performing comprehensive quality control audits, conducting detailed annual escrow analyses, and monitoring workflow queues to maintain data integrity. Acts as the escalation point for complex escrow discrepancies, collaborating cross-functionally with loan servicing, compliance, and accounting teams to resolve high-priority exceptions, mitigate operational and financial risk, and ensure strict adherence to state, federal, and RESPA guidelines.

Essential Responsibilities:

  • (25%) Operational & Quality Assurance Oversight. Monitors, reviews, and validates daily escrow operations to ensure the accurate tracking and timely disbursement of real estate property taxes, homeowners’ insurance, and flood insurance. Performs regular quality control audits on escrow accounts and workflow queues to identify discrepancies, correct data errors, and maintain integrity across the mortgage servicing system. Serves as the primary operational contact for routine functions, validating system records against real estate tax authority and insurance carrier requirements to ensure seamless processing.
  • (20%) Exception Management & Complex Issue Resolution. Serves as the primary escalation point for complex discrepancies, title updates, tax sale warnings, and insurance policy lapses or cancellations. Investigates and resolves high-priority exceptions, tax refunds, missing bills, and insurance draft claims in direct coordination with borrowers and property agents. Conducts root-cause analysis on recurring account errors to continuously improve internal operational controls, reduce financial risk, and refine workflow procedures.
  • (20%) Escrow Analysis & Account Adjustments. Performs, reviews, and issues accurate annual escrow analyses for mortgage accounts in full compliance with Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA) regulations. Calculates account shortages, surpluses, deficiencies to establish adjusted monthly escrow payment amounts, ensuring changes are communicated clearly to members. Executes account recalculations resulting from tax re-assessments or insurance policy cost adjustments, maintaining proper account balancing and ledger corrections throughout the loan lifecycle.
  • (15%) Member Service & Stakeholder Support. Provides support and subject-matter expertise to members, third parties, and internal credit union teams regarding complex escrow inquiries and statement details. Drafts, updates, and distributes member notices. Collaborates cross-functionally with Loan Servicing, Accounting, Legal, And Compliance departments to address member escalations promptly and maintain high service standards.
  • (10%) Loss Drafts & Special Property Processing. Administers loss draft insurance claims from initiation to resolution, which includes monitoring repair progress, managing escrow-held claim disbursements, and verifying final property restoration completion. Tracks special property requirements across the real estate portfolio, ensuring continuous oversight for mandatory flood zone monitoring and dynamic local property tax assessment cycles.
  • (10 %) Compliance, Reporting, & Audit Support. Prepares and analyzes weekly, monthly, and annual escrow department reports to track disbursement status, unearned premiums, and active exception queues. Ensures strict adherence to federal, state, and RESPA guidelines concerning statutory timeframes, borrower notification periods, interest payments, and recordkeeping requirements. Assists internal and external auditors during periodic compliance reviews by gathering necessary documentation, reports, and sample account files.

Required Education & Experience (Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities):

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Real Estate, Accounting or related field. Additional 2 years of relevant experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
  • ​​​2+ years Loan Servicing and/or Escrow experience
  • Must have knowledge of loan servicing procedures.
  • Comprehensive understanding of Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA) guidelines, escrow account mechanics, annual escrow analyses, real estate property taxes, and homeowners/flood insurance policies.
  • High degree of proficiency in mathematical calculations, financial ledger balancing, root-cause error analysis, and auditing complex account balances.
  • Intermediate to advanced skill level with mortgage servicing software systems, document management platforms, database tools, and Microsoft Office Suite (particularly Excel and Word).

Preferred Education & Experience (Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities):

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Real Estate, Accounting, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in mortgage escrow servicing, real estate tax administration, or hazard/flood insurance compliance within a bank, credit union, or mortgage institution.

Job Environment & Physical Requirements:

  • Office setting with hybrid possibility (based on performance)
  • Must be able to comprehend and carry out verbal and written instructions.
  • Must be able to comprehend phone calls.
  • Must be able to lift 5 pounds.

title: Director, Business Program Management Office
description:
The Company

Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ DXCM) is a pioneer and global leader in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Dexcom began as a small company with a big dream: To forever change how diabetes is managed. To unlock information and insights that drive better health outcomes. Here we are 25 years later, having pioneered an industry. And we're just getting started. We are broadening our vision beyond diabetes to empower people to take control of health. That means personalized, actionable insights aimed at solving important health challenges. To continue what we've started: Improving human health.

We are driven by thousands of ambitious, passionate people worldwide who are willing to fight like warriors to earn the trust of our customers by listening, serving with integrity, thinking big, and being dependable. We've already changed millions of lives and we're ready to change millions more. Our future ambition is to become a leading consumer health technology company while continuing to develop solutions for serious health conditions. We'll get there by constantly reinventing unique biosensing-technology experiences. Though we've come a long way from our small company days, our dreams are bigger than ever. The opportunity to improve health on a global scale stands before us.


Meet the team:

Dexcom is seeking a strategic, enterprise-minded leader to establish and lead a globally integrated Business PMO that enables scalable execution, disciplined governance, and measurable business impact across the enterprise. This role will provide executive-level leadership for complex, global, cross-functional process and technology initiatives, partnering closely with Finance, IT, global operations, commercial teams, and delivery centers to drive alignment, accountability, and value realization. The mandate: turn enterprise priorities into a managed portfolio, point scarce capacity at the work that moves the business, and hold the governance that carries an idea from discussion to decision to delivery.

You will build the operating model, program standards, governance mechanisms, and executive reporting required to manage a global portfolio of high-priority initiatives, including enterprise process transformation. Specifically partnering with IT & the business to deliver ERP and platform implementations, AI-enabled operating improvements, and cost and productivity programs. The leader will ensure programs are structured to deliver clear outcomes, manage risk, support business readiness, and sustain adoption across large, matrixed environments. You will work across Finance, IT, Commercial, Operations, Quality, Regulatory, Product, and Delivery centers to sequence priorities, manage dependencies, settle trade-offs, and land adoption in the business.

Success in this position requires the ability to translate enterprise priorities into actionable program roadmaps, mobilize stakeholders across functions and regions, and establish the governance, decision forums, and operating cadence needed to drive consistent execution. You will separate activity from value, surface risks early & make executive decisions easier giving Dexcom the capability to execute change with speed, transparency and confidence.

Where you come in:

  • You will establish and lead a globally integrated Business PMO, including the operating model, governance, intake, stage-gates standards, tools, and executive reporting needed to manage a complex enterprise portfolio.
  • You will lead large-scale, cross-functional transformation programs across business processes, technology platforms & commercial operations, ensuring clear outcomes, disciplined execution, and measurable value realization.
  • You will partner closely with Finance, IT, Commercial, Operations, Quality, Regulatory, and global delivery centers to align priorities, resolve dependencies, manage risks, and accelerate decision-making.
  • You will translate enterprise strategy into actionable program roadmaps, integrated plans, milestones, resource requirements, and success measures to ensure consistent portfolio management and change-control mechanisms that drive transparency, prioritization, accountability, and delivery confidence across programs.
  • You will partner with IT and business leaders on platform enabled change across ERP, AI-enabled workflows, and data products with business readiness and continuity built into the project plans.
  • You will develop executive-ready updates, recommendations, and decision materials for senior governance forums, including clear reporting on status, risks, dependencies, decision logs, escalation triggers, financial impact, portfolio health reporting and value delivery.
  • You will lead and develop a high-performing, multidisciplinary team across program management, governance, analytics, business readiness, and benefit realization, building scalable capability for future enterprise initiatives.
  • You will build the PMO capability across the organization working in partnership with functional PMOs to ensure consistency in approach, methodology, priorities and structures to ensure a singular view of initiatives and activities is achievable at a Executive level.

What makes you successful:

  • You bring deep experience leading large-scale global or enterprise transformation programs, ideally within complex, regulated, and matrixed organizations.
  • You have built or led PMO, transformation, or enterprise program governance functions at scale, with a strong track record of improving execution discipline, transparency, and business outcomes – turning strategy into an executable portfolio.
  • You combine strategic thinking with operational rigor, translating enterprise priorities into clear roadmaps, governance mechanisms, success measures, and sustained value realization.
  • You are highly effective in ambiguity and complexity, creating structure, simplifying priorities, and helping senior leaders make timely, evidence-based decisions.
  • You influence across functions and regions without relying on direct authority, aligning stakeholders with demonstrated experience operating through influence without direct control.
  • You have strong business, financial, technology, and process acumen, and have delivered ERP or platform-enabled transformation, enterprise business processes, automation, AI-enabled improvements, and data-driven decision-making.
  • You understand change management and business readiness, including how to anticipate resistance, drive adoption, and embed new ways of working across large teams.
  • You develop strong teams and organizational capability, fostering accountability, inclusion, learning, and continuous improvement.

What makes you successful:

  • One visible enterprise portfolio with consistent intake, prioritization, governance, reporting, risk management, and value tracking.
  • Faster executive decisions, backed by concise portfolio health reporting, decision logs, trade-off recommendations, and escalation discipline.
  • Higher delivery confidence on priority programs through standard milestones, stage gates, readiness checks, and dependency management.
  • Value realization measured across revenue, margin, cost, risk, reliability, customer experience, and productivity, validated with Finance.
  • A PMO bench that operates as business partners and transformation leaders.

What you’ll get:

  • A front row seat to life changing CGM technology. Learn about our brave #dexcomwarriors community.
  • A full and comprehensive benefits program.
  • Growth opportunities on a global scale.
  • Access to career development through in-house learning programs and/or qualified tuition reimbursement.
  • An exciting and innovative, industry-leading organization committed to our employees, customers, and the communities we serve.

  • 13+ years of industry experience
  • 5-8 years of previous people management experience

Job Description

Schedule: Wednesday/Thursday 1pm-5pm, Friday/Saturday 1pm-5:30pm, Sunday 11am-3:30am (21.5 hours per week)

Position Summary:

The Kitchen Worker provides operational support for a high-volume operation while ensuring proper sanitation, efficient practices, and compliance with food handling standards. The Kitchen Worker provides a wide range of support including, but not limited to food preparation, dish and ware washing, maintaining cleanliness and trash removal, serving food, and stocking as necessary. This position is part of the success of the food service program serving food through dining halls, cafes, catering, and a food truck. The Kitchen Worker follows Health Department regulations and expectations of Vassar College with regards to food quality, safety, preparation, presentation, and audit compliance.

Responsibilities:

  • As directed by the management team, complete tasks that contribute to the Dining Services daily operation.

  • Perform quality work and meet deadlines for meals as assigned by the culinary and management teams.

  • Assemble salads and sandwiches using pre-cooked or ready-to-eat ingredients, prepare protein-based salads such as tuna salad, and chop, organize, and prepare ingredients to be used for service or for the overall food production effort.

  • Properly and safely use various knives to cut and prepare food ingredients with precision and efficiency

  • Serve food according to food safety guidelines and monitor for freshness and quality.

  • Understanding of FIFO principles with daily rotation of stock and properly date/label products stored in coolers, dry storage, or kitchen areas in proper storage containers.

  • Capacity to operate all of the stations and platforms throughout the dining operation within classification.

  • As the runner, gather ingredients and ice from coolers, freezers and stock rooms for efficient food production and service.

  • Throughout the duration of a shift, at the conclusion of a shift, and in preparation for service the next day, ensure kitchen surfaces including floors as well as equipment, pots, pans and utensils dishes, and flatware are maintained, cleaned, sanitized, and organized appropriately to expected standards.

  • Responsible for the proper use of the dish room equipment using water softener and dish washing chemical disbursement to clean, scrape, wash, and stack dishes, utensils, and cooking equipment.

  • Execute utility functions such as, but not limited to sweeping, mopping, cleaning up spills, trash removal, compostable collection, breaking down boxes, proper collection of recyclables including cardboard, and cleaning and sanitizing carts and trash receptacles and trash collection areas as needed.

  • Clean and sanitize stations, tables, and counters throughout the operation. Restock dishes, flatware, pots, pans, cups, glasses and utensils. Refill napkin baskets, condiments, and salt/pepper shakers as needed.

  • Make coffee and refill milks, sweeteners, juices, soda, C02, and ensure the beverage areas remain clean and sanitary.

  • Restock open air coolers and serving areas with product, fruit, and other items as needed. Assist with putting chairs on tables at the end of the night.

  • Operate and safely use equipment necessary for the job including dish room equipment, assigned kitchen equipment and elevators.

Required knowledge, skills and abilities:

  • Ability to lift heavy objects up to 50 pounds and frequently lift and push, pull or carry up to 30 pounds. Team lift anything greater than 50 pounds.

  • Ability to stand and walk for the duration of a shift using repetitive motion with your upper body to complete tasks.

  • Communicate effectively in English including understanding speaking, reading and writing.

  • Remain within work deployment for the duration of a shift except for scheduled breaks and meal periods.

  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with staff, students/customers, and management. Serve customers in an efficient and friendly manner while resolving any potential issues, remaining flexible to last minute adjustments, and/or by promptly reporting issues to management.

  • Must help ensure success of the dining program by following Health Department regulations and food safety standards as laid out by Vassar and Vassar’s food contract management company.

  • Use necessary protective equipment per guidelines from Vassar and Vassar’s food contract management company.

  • Properly direct and refer questions as it relates to HACCP principles in the field of sanitation and cooking, and allergen and celiac disease.

Preferred knowledge, skills and abilities:

  • 1 year of professional food service experience in a high-volume food service environment.

  • Certification in the National Restaurant Association’s ServSafe course for food safety.

  • Willingness to work overtime when available, as assigned according to seniority guidelines.

Pay Rate: $21.39 per hour

title: QC Technician I
description:
At Sensient Technologies, we are experts in the science, art and innovation of color and flavor. We are market-savvy and visionary. We are problem solvers. And we will be better with you.

We are looking for a Quality Control Tech I to join our team in Harbor Beach, MI. The QC Tech will analyze various critical parameters of processes and products to ensure that the facility is efficiently producing high quality products. Individuals will understand and effectively utilize calibration procedures, aseptic technique, basic process control as well as troubleshoot analytical equipment problems during the night production shift.

What you’ll do

  • Conduct a variety of tests on raw materials and finished products, including texture, moisture, pH, salt levels, and acidity
  • Perform microbiological analyses such as plate counts and swabbing procedures
  • Use precise techniques to support the calibration and upkeep of lab instruments
  • Document and interpret test results while maintaining clear, accurate records
  • Assist with reviewing materials for quality compliance and managing inventory status
  • Help organize and facilitate sensory panels to evaluate product characteristics
  • Collaborate with team members to support process improvements and maintain standards

What you’ll bring

  • A keen eye for detail and a methodical approach to tasks
  • Interest or background in laboratory or scientific work, particularly in food, chemical, or microbiological testing
  • Willingness to follow established procedures and help troubleshoot simple equipment issues
  • Ability to stay focused and organized while juggling multiple testing responsibilities
  • Comfort with basic math, measurement, and documentation along with clear communication skills to interact with both team members and supervisors
  • A degree in a scientific field is helpful, but not required – training will be provided

What you’ll get

  • A stable role in a respected company focused on quality and innovation
  • Hands-on training in laboratory techniques and quality processes
  • A structured, supportive environment where your accuracy and commitment matter
  • The chance to contribute to products that people use and enjoy every day
  • Access to tools, equipment, and learning opportunities to grow your skills
  • A reliable schedule and a team that values consistency and collaboration
  • Competitive pay and benefits designed to support your well-being

About Sensient:

Sensient Technologies Corporation is a leading global manufacturer and marketer of colors, flavors, and extracts. Sensient employs advanced technologies at facilities around the world to develop specialty food and beverage systems, cosmetic and pharmaceutical systems, specialty colors, and other specialty and fine chemicals. The Company's customers include major international manufacturers representing most of the world's best-known brands.

About Sensient Flavors:

Sensient Flavors offers innovative, global taste solutions and specialized flavor delivery systems that help bring life to your food and beverage products. Our leading-edge technologies reflect our core philosophies to be dynamic and innovative and to add value to your applications.

title: Division Chair - Commercial Contracting
description:
Provides executive leadership of Mayo Clinic's strategies for commercial payer contracts to deliver patient care services and participate in provider networks which total more than $13 billion on an annual basis. Responsible for managing contract activities for all Mayo sites, payers, and programs. Oversees relationships with many types of entities including insurance companies, managed care plans, employers/corporations, business coalitions, high value/COE networks, and even governmental entities.

Also responsible for certain assigned functional activity, contracting programs, and/or service lines across all sites. Functions, programs, and service lines can include product development; transplant contracting; specialty network contracting; government contracting; direct employer contracting; national payer contracting; international contracting; population health contracting; payer financial analytics; contract financial support; healthcare promotions; and various liaison roles.

The Division Chair and its direct reports negotiate financial terms of key contracts directly with payers’ senior level management. Responsible for financial performance of contract portfolio for site and assigned functions/programs/service lines.

Responsible for collaborating with physicians, practice administrative, and finance leaders to ensure contracting strategies and activities support the practice/site, strategic initiatives, and financial models. Serves as institutional resource and educates Mayo leadership regarding managed care contracts, payer markets, and competitive trends. Serves as a primary Revenue Strategies and Innovation contact and collaborator for site Administrators, Physician CEOs/Leaders, and CFOs for commercial contracting.

Position Responsibilities:

  • Leads, organizes and maintains an effective contracting team which results in Mayo practices being an attractive provider of health services for payers, including strategies to market distinct services available at Mayo practices

  • Works collaboratively with Chair, RSI, to provide leadership in commercial contracting area, ensuring Mayo Clinic leaders are informed with regular market surveillance, aware of contracting strategies and new developments, and engaged as new initiatives are considered.

  • Develops and maintains strong and positive relationships with all strategically important commercial payers, ensuring they are aware of new clinical programs and services available, Mayo Clinic’s core value proposition(s), includes multiple connection points (CEO, CMO, and Rev Cycle in addition to RSI) between Mayo Clinic and each payer organization.

  • Oversees the development and execution of commercial payer contracting strategies and initiatives, including specific clinical department objectives that support overall organizational contracting strategies.

  • Seeks support and input from Clinical Practice Committee, Executive Operations Team, Board of Governors, and other leadership bodies for strategies.

  • Works collaboratively with Clinical Practice Committee’s (CPC's), Department/Division Chairs and others to assure appropriate clinical input to commercial contracting activities.

  • Works collaboratively with internal administrative (Finance; Revenue Cycle; Marketing; Planning; Legal) and Practice (Executive Health) areas in the development of new initiatives and to address operational objectives.

  • Develops an internal organization that is deeply committed to customer service, continuous improvement and manages internal operations to ensure efficient performance.

  • Implement policies and procedures to communicate contract terms to appropriate Mayo staff. Ensures sufficient support documentation is in contract files.

This is a hybrid position and must be located within 100 miles of one of the following Mayo Clinic campuses: Jacksonville, FL; Phoenix, AZ; or Rochester, MN, with an expectation to work on-site based on business needs.

Ten (10) years’ experience in provider-payer contracting with a track record of success and similar health care finance or administration with demonstrated leadership skills is required. Bachelors’ degree, preferably in a business-related field is required. An MBA, MHA or other relevant Master’s degree is preferred. A strong foundation and familiarity with healthcare financing, billing/claims, and negotiation strategies is necessary.

Required skills include (a) Strategic thought leadership with ability to lead contracting teams; (b) Excellent communications and interpersonal relations skills, including negotiating skills, to build and sustain positive working relationship with commercial payer executives as well as internal Mayo leadership; (c) Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills to strategically assess contract performance and impact of trends and developments in health care on Mayo Clinic’s contracted revenue; and (d) Enthusiasm for collaboration with and across payer boundaries to advance holistic strategies for Mayo Clinic’s entire revenue stream.

C.P.A. if position is focused on finance. FSA/ASA (Society of Actuaries) or AAA (Member, Amer. Academy of Actuaries) designations could be considered as an alternative to a C.P.A.

title: Agente de Seguridad (Security Officer) - Amanvari
description:
Location Overview

Join our team at Amanvari. A remote natural paradise on Mexico’s Eastern Cape, Aman’s newest retreat finds home between the Sierra de la Laguna mountains and the calm waters of the Sea of Cortés. Echoing its name, a combination of the Sanskrit-derived words for ‘peace’ and ‘water,’ Amanvari rests in harmony with its exclusive yet inspiring setting, an exclusive 1,000-acre community just one hour from Los Cabos International airport.

Rol

El Agente de Seguridad es responsable de mantener un ambiente seguro y protegido para todos los huéspedes, colegas y visitantes dentro del Hotel. Este puesto garantiza que todas las políticas de seguridad, protección y prevención de pérdidas se implementen de manera efectiva, y que todos los incidentes sean atendidos con prontitud y profesionalismo. El Agente de Seguridad desempeñará funciones preventivas y reactivas, demostrando los más altos estándares de discreción, integridad y servicio al huésped, alineados con la filosofía de paz y privacidad de Aman.

Role

The Security Officer is responsible for maintaining a safe and secure environment for all guests, colleagues, and visitors throughout the resort. This role ensures that all security, safety, and loss prevention policies are effectively implemented and that all incidents are handled promptly and professionally. The Security Officer will perform both preventive and reactive duties, demonstrating the highest standards of discretion, integrity, and guest service aligned with Aman’s philosophy of peace and privacy.

Responsabilidades Principales

  • Monitorear y patrullar todas las áreas del resort para prevenir, detectar y responder a incidentes de seguridad y de seguridad ocupacional.

  • Operar y observar los sistemas de CCTV para identificar comportamientos inusuales, actividades sospechosas o situaciones de riesgo.

  • Apoyar la implementación de los procedimientos de seguridad del hotel, las respuestas a emergencias y los planes de evacuación.

  • Realizar investigaciones sobre pérdidas, robos, accidentes o daños a la propiedad, elaborando reportes precisos y detallados.

  • Asistir en el control de acceso a áreas restringidas y garantizar el uso adecuado de gafetes de identificación.

  • Responder de manera rápida y calmada a alarmas, emergencias y llamadas de asistencia de los huéspedes.

  • Reportar de inmediato al Supervisor de Seguridad cualquier equipo de seguridad defectuoso o con fallas.

  • Apoyar el mantenimiento de los sistemas de seguridad, incluyendo detección de incendios, extintores y salidas de emergencia.

  • Participar activamente en simulacros de seguridad, sesiones de entrenamiento y reuniones diarias del departamento.

  • Mantener la limpieza, organización y confidencialidad dentro de la oficina de seguridad y la sala de control de CCTV.

  • Relacionarse de manera profesional con los huéspedes, demostrando empatía y serenidad en todas las interacciones.

  • Colaborar con otros departamentos para garantizar operaciones seguras y una respuesta efectiva ante incidentes.

  • Promover la cultura de conciencia y seguridad proactiva de Aman dentro de la propiedad.

  • Observar y hacer cumplir todas las políticas del hotel, incluidas las relacionadas con la conservación de energía, seguridad laboral y código de conducta.

  • Realizar otras tareas asignadas por el Director de Seguridad.

Key Responsibilities

  • Monitor and patrol all resort areas to prevent, detect, and respond to security and safety incidents.

  • Operate and observe CCTV systems to identify unusual behavior, suspicious activities, or safety concerns.

  • Support the implementation of hotel security procedures, emergency responses, and evacuation plans.

  • Conduct investigations into loss, theft, accidents, or property damage, preparing accurate and detailed reports.

  • Assist in controlling access to restricted areas and ensure the proper use of identification badges.

  • Respond promptly and calmly to alarms, emergencies, and guest calls for assistance.

  • Report defective or malfunctioning security equipment to the Security Supervisor immediately.

  • Support the maintenance of safety systems including fire detection, fire extinguishers, and emergency exits.

  • Participate actively in safety drills, training sessions, and daily departmental briefings.

  • Maintain cleanliness, organization, and confidentiality within the security office and CCTV control room.

  • Liaise professionally with guests, demonstrating empathy and composure in all interactions.

  • Collaborate with other departments to ensure safe operations and effective response to incidents.

  • Promote Aman’s culture of awareness and proactive safety within the property.

  • Observe and enforce all hotel policies, including those related to energy conservation, workplace safety, and code of conduct.

Perfil del Candidato

  • Mínimo un (1) año de experiencia en un puesto similar, preferiblemente en hospitalidad de lujo.

  • Diploma de preparatoria o educación equivalente requerida.

  • Dominio intermedio o avanzado del idioma inglés (mínimo 75%)

  • Certificación o formación como Paramédico, Primer Respondiente o en Primeros Auxilios Avanzados (CPR, AED, atención a trauma).

  • Fuertes habilidades de observación y elaboración de reportes; capaz de manejar información confidencial con discreción.

  • Excelente condición física y disponibilidad para trabajar horarios flexibles, incluyendo noches y fines de semana.

  • Capacidad para trabajar en equipo, con actitud calmada, integridad y buenas habilidades interpersonales.

  • Conocimientos en respuesta a emergencias, primeros auxilios y prevención de incendios son preferibles.

  • Manejo básico de computadoras y familiaridad con sistemas de CCTV es una ventaja.

Qualifications

  • Minimum one (1) year of experience in a similar role, preferably in luxury hospitality.

  • High school diploma or equivalent education required.

  • Intermediate to Advanced proficiency in English (minimum 75%).

  • Certification or training as a Paramedic, First Responder, or in Advanced First Aid (CPR, AED, trauma care).

  • Strong observation and reporting abilities; capable of handling confidential information with discretion.

  • Excellent physical condition and the ability to work flexible schedules, including nights and weekends.

  • Team player with a calm demeanor, integrity, and strong interpersonal skills.

  • Knowledge of emergency response, first aid, and fire prevention procedures preferred.

  • Computer literacy and familiarity with CCTV systems are an advantage.

title: AI Cyber Risk and Credible Challenge Associate Director
description:
Are you ready to make an impact at DTCC?

Do you want to work on innovative projects, collaborate with a dynamic and supportive team, and receive investment in your professional development? At DTCC, we are at the forefront of innovation in the financial markets. We're committed to helping our employees grow and succeed. We believe that you have the skills and drive to make a real impact. We foster a thriving internal community and are committed to creating a workplace that looks like the world that we serve.

Pay and Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation, including base pay and annual incentive
  • Comprehensive health and life insurance and well-being benefits, based on location
  • Pension / Retirement benefits
  • Paid Time Off and Personal/Family Care, and other leaves of absence when needed to support your physical, financial, and emotional well-being.
  • DTCC offers a flexible/hybrid model of 3 days onsite and 2 days remote (onsite Tuesdays, Wednesdays and a third day unique to each team or employee).

The Impact You will have in this role:

In this role, you will play a key part in executing the Credible Challenge assessment program within the Cyber Security Risk Office (CSRO), with a specialized focus on AI risk oversight across the AI lifecycle. Your work will directly contribute to strengthening DTCC’s cyber risk governance by independently assessing First Line functions and evaluating the design and effectiveness of controls.
You will work closely with CSRO leadership, assessment leads, and First Line stakeholders to perform structured assessments, analyze evidence, identify risks and control gaps, and support clear, defensible assessment conclusions.

Your Primary Responsibilities:

  • Lead and execute Credible Challenge assessments of First Line AI risk practices across the AI lifecycle, including planning, scoping, fieldwork, and documentation
  • Perform walkthroughs, interviews, and evidence reviews to assess the design and operating effectiveness of controls governing AI use cases (including GenAI, agentic workflows, and embedded AI)
  • Evaluate alignment of First Line AI practices to the AI Policy, AI Governance Procedure, AI Acceptable Usage Policy, and applicable frameworks (NIST AI RMF, CRI Profile, EU AI Act)
  • Represent CSRO on the AI Working Groups, conducting independent AI use case reviews and applying the AI risk tiering framework to scale challenge intensity to data exposure, automation, and business impact
  • Identify, assess, and communicate material AI risks, control gaps, and thematic issues across cyber, model, data, privacy, and third-party risk domains
  • Engage with senior CSRO and First Line stakeholders to discuss assessment results and remediation of AI control deficiencies
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of the Credible Challenge methodology, standards, and templates as applied to the AI domain
  • Support AI policy awareness and acceptable-usage training, and assist with regulatory and audit responses on AI (e.g., Reg SCI, FRBNY/SEC inquiries)
  • Lead and contribute to special projects including program enhancements, resource coordination, and senior management presentations
  • Develop, communicate and ensure adherence to department risk policies, procedures and best practices
  • Stay abreast of industry and market events that impact cyber risk management processes
  • Foster an environment of regulatory awareness and ensure regulatory compliance
  • Conduct periodic assessments and surveys to gauge DTCC's AI risk and acceptable usage awareness level and recommend adjustments to the program

Staff Geologist (Remote, Up to 75% Travel)

This Staff Geologist ensures the delivery of high-quality spring water collected in compliance with FDA/IBWA requirements and maintains up-to-date and readily accessible information on Niagara-utilized spring sources. The role will manage the evaluation and qualification of new spring and water well sources for expansion plants and as back up sources for existing facilities.

This position reports to the Principal Geologist.

Detailed Description - The Staff Geologist shall do, or supervise the Geologist I and II positions in doing, the following:

Technical Management and Monitoring of Niagara-Utilized Spring Sources.

  • Be the primary point of contact for, and liaison to spring source owners fostering professional working relationships
  • Maintain routine contact with all spring owners.
  • Conduct as-needed, spring source audits to ensure compliance with Niagara operating requirements
  • Monitor overall spring source water quality and any changes or trends over time
  • Track spring source permits, expirations and renewals
  • Develop and maintain database/documentation supporting spring SOI, hydrogeology, engineering and permits
  • Be a technical resource to spring owners as they upgrade or modify their facilities
  • Track regulatory changes pertaining to spring sources
  • Maintain awareness of land use activities and potential contaminant threats in the vicinity of the spring sources
  • Be the Niagara representative at regulatory and local community meetings (when necessary)
  • Partner in spring improvement work under a cost-recovery agreement with the spring owner where appropriate an in conjunction with the Procurement team

Evaluate New Spring Water Sources for Expansion Projects and Ongoing Operations.

  • Work with the Procurement and Expansion teams to identify spring sources in the vicinity of proposed Expansion facilities
  • Evaluate the technical merits and viability of prospect spring sources
  • Assist with spring site development layout/design
  • Prepare planning cost estimates for improvements that may be necessary to bring prospect springs online
  • Provide technical support to Niagara's Contracts Team
  • Seek/develop opportunities for Niagara-owned spring sources

Spring Source Information System

  • Work with staff to build database information on each spring source
  • Maintain the water quality data base and provide statistics and graphing trends for spring sources when needed

Technical Management of Niagara-Owned Groundwater Water Supply Wells

  • Water well siting, design, permitting, drilling and installation; testing and maintenance
  • Aquifer testing and water quality sampling
  • Documentation and report preparation

  • A mindset focused on quality, problem-solving, and openness to new ideas.
  • Team-oriented approach – willing to pitch in, learn, and lead by example.

title: Survey Data Processor
description:
EBC thinks outside the box and deploys all its know-how to carry out major infrastructure projects: bridges, roads, highways, tunnels, marine installations, wind farms, and hydroelectric projects. Our ability to meet deadlines and budgets as well as our vast expertise in the field allow us to actively participate in large-scale projects such as the Site C hydro-electric power station located near Fort St-John in British Columbia, the Samuel-De-Champlain Bridge, and the Réseau Express Métropolitain (REM). EBC is positioned as a true leader in this sector. Our range of specialized services has made our reputation in Canada.

EBC Inc. is seeking a Survey Data Processor for our Mississauga Office.

The Survey Data Processor supports construction projects by preparing layout files, analyzing technical data, and producing accurate deliverables used in the field. This role works closely with surveyors, modelers, and site teams to ensure precision, consistency, and reliability of survey and layout information throughout the project lifecycle.

Responsibilities
  • Create layout and implantation files for construction sites.
  • Read, interpret, and analyze plans, specifications, sections and profiles.
  • Analyze and extract data from 3D models provided by designers or modelers.
  • Process, organize, and validate data collected by Field Surveyors and remote-controlled and automated machinery.
  • Produce technical deliverables, including layout and construction plans and quantity tracking, work progress tracking, technical validations, as-built drawings, etc.
  • Apply knowledge of field data collection methods, including file naming conventions, point numbering systems, project point codes, identification of critical elements to be surveyed, etc.
  • Provide technical support to the Chief Surveyor for complex calculation methods.
  • Collaborate closely with modelers to support and fulfill technical requirements.


Requirements

  • Minimum 5 years of experience in the construction and/or surveying field.
  • Strong understanding of construction site realities and survey operations.
  • Proven experience working with technical data, calculations, and layout processes.

Desired Profile & Core Competencies
  • High level of rigor and precision.
  • Strong focus on data accuracy and calculation reliability.
  • Ability to work independently on complex technical tasks.
  • Strong sense of responsibility when handling critical project data.
  • Ability to work closely with Field Surveyors, Modelers, Chief Surveyor and Construction site teams.
  • Capable of clearly explaining technical methods and requirements.
  • Ability to transition between technical calculations, field support, coordination and documentation
  • Flexible and responsive to evolving project and site demands.

  • RRSP group program with an employer contribution to a DPSP.
  • Employee assistance program.
  • Continuing education.
  • Active social club.

title: Senior Network Engineer
description:
Summary

Under the supervision of the IT Manager, the Senior Network Engineer is responsible for the design, implementation, configuration, and optimization of our enterprise network infrastructure across data centers, branch sites, and cloud environments. Ideal candidates will have deep experience with nextgen firewalls, routers, switches, Wireless Access Points, plus a strong command of WAN routing protocols, SD-WAN, IDS/IPS, VPNs, and Firewall ACLs.

  1. Architecture & Design: Build resilient network architectures (campus, WAN/SD-WAN, data centers), segmentation, policy-based routing, and high-availability frameworks.

  7. Leadership: Lead multi-site tech projects and mentor junior staff.

title: DFIR Engineer II - Incident Response
description:
About the Job:

As a DFIR Engineer II on the Threat Detection & Response team, your role will include responding to, investigating and containing anomalous or malicious activity that could indicate a security threat. You’ll be responsible for staying up to date on the latest cybersecurity threats and assisting in the continual development and refinement related to monitoring, detecting and responding to abnormal network and host activity.

What You'll Do:

  • Triage, pivot and correlate across multiple network and host-based log sources.
  • Analyze system artifacts and memory for evidence of compromise.
  • Proactively hunt for and identify malicious activity in various log sources using threat intelligence and other indicators of compromise.
  • Document detailed findings including timelines of events or incidents
  • Continually improve incident response procedures and documentation.
  • Engage with Detection Engineering and Red Team to identify opportunities to better monitor/detect suspicious behavior and automate response capabilities.
  • Keep up to date on evolving cyber threats and identify methods to detect them.
  • Participate in an on-call rotation with other Incident Response Engineers

What Skills You'll Bring :

  • Experience with security tools including SIEM, EDR, AV, CASB, Next-gen Firewalls, and VPN.
  • Experience with system and network artifacts.
  • Working knowledge of the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
  • Familiarity with various cloud environments and containerization technologies (AWS, Azure, O365, Docker, Kubernetes).
  • Functional and practical experience with at least one development or scripting language/framework (e.g. PowerShell, Python, .Net) and regular expressions.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Demonstrated curiosity and passion for cybersecurity.

Everyone Is a Caregiver

At UMass Memorial Health, everyone is a caregiver – regardless of their title or responsibilities. Exceptional patient care, academic excellence and leading-edge research make UMass Memorial the premier health system of Central Massachusetts, and a place where we can help you build the career you deserve. We are more than 20,000 employees, working together as one health system in a relentless pursuit of healing for our patients, community and each other. And everyone, in their own unique way, plays an important part, every day.

Under the direction of the appropriate licensed clinician, the Patient Care Technician I performs a variety of patient care activities. Receives workplace education and training to assist members of the healthcare team in the care of patients.

I. Major Responsibilities:
1. Provides clear, timely communication to the RN regarding observations and changes seen in patients. Examples, but not limited to changes in skin condition, vital signs, and/or mental status.
2. Provides constant observation of high-risk patients as assigned by the Resource Nurse or designee.
3. Participates in the development and maintenance of a safe environment. Works to utilize interventions to de-escalate patients and if unsuccessful participates in restraints in accordance with training and education as directed.
4. Assists patient with daily living activities such as personal hygiene, ambulating, meals and nourishment.
5. Assists in moving, lifting, positioning, and transporting patients by utilizing proper safety techniques and body mechanics in all work-related activities.
6. Maintains patient safety by performing patient safety checks, utilizing fall prevention alternative devices/strategies as directed, and following the Restraint Policy standards when caring for a restrained patient.
7. Takes and records vital signs (temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure and pulse oxymetry). Measures and records patients’ weights and heights.
8. Performs EKG’s, Point of Care (POC) tests and bladder scanning. Collects, labels and prepares specimens for transport to lab.
9. Performs other selected unit specific procedures, such as battery changes for telemetry units, checking status of unit equipment, cleaning equipment between patients and proper storage of supplies.
10. Assists RN/Licensed Independent Practitioner with treatments and procedures by preparing patient, obtaining equipment and supplies, helping to position patient, providing the patient with emotional support, and cleaning up equipment and supplies following the treatment and/or procedure.
11. Observes, measures, records oral food and fluid intake. Refills tube feeding bags as directed. Empties and records output, as approved, from a variety of sources, e.g., foley catheter, ostomy appliances and drainage systems. Performs ostomy care on established ostomate patients as directed.
12. Demonstrates sensitivity and responsiveness to patients’ needs by acting as a source of information and approaches all interactions with the intention of building positive rapport and relationships.
13. Provides respectful, culturally and age-appropriate communication with patients, staff, family, visitors and others.
14. Replenishes patient and unit supplies and equipment as needed.
15. Requests assistance from identified resources when more direction is needed.
16. Keeps current with hospital and unit changes by reading communication boards and/or books, bulletin boards, posted notices and reads and responds to UMMHC e mails on a regular basis.
 
Standard Staffing Level Responsibilities:
1. Complies with established departmental policies, procedures, and objectives.
2. Attends variety of meetings, conferences, seminars as required or directed.
3. Demonstrates use of Quality Improvement in daily operations.
4. Complies with all health and safety regulations and requirements.
5. Respects diverse views and approaches, demonstrates Standards of Respect, and contributes to creating and maintaining an environment of professionalism, tolerance, civility and acceptance toward all employees, patients, and visitors.
6. Maintains, regular, reliable, and predictable attendance.
7. Performs other similar and related duties as required or directed.

All responsibilities are essential job functions.

II. Position Qualifications:

License/Certification/Education:

Required:

1. Minimum of a high school education or GED.
2. Basic Life Support certification within 30-days as a condition of employment.

Experience/Skills:

Required:
1. Ability to read, write and communicate in English in a clear and concise manner.
2. Basic computer skills
3. Basic Medical Terminology knowledge.
4. Must be able to remain calm when under stress or in emergency situations

Unless certification, licensure or registration is required, an equivalent combination of education and experience which provides proficiency in the areas of responsibility listed in this description may be substituted for the above requirements.
Department-specific competencies and their measurements will be developed and maintained in the individual departments. The competencies will be maintained and attached to the departmental job description. Responsible managers will review competencies with position incumbents.

III. Physical Demands and Environmental Conditions:
Position requires work indoors in a patient care environment.
Hand dexterity, hearing and vision ability to take direction from a patient or provider, adjust equipment, observe and describe patient observations. Must be able to lift, up to 50 pounds.
Work is of heavy demand, standing and walking most of the time with the possibility of pushing heavy equipment and bending frequently.

title: General Repair Technician III
description:
SUMMARY
Technician III is responsible for operating the facility including, but not limited to mechanical other supporting systems; performing structured inspections, preventative and corrective maintenance, routine and on-demand services on facility mechanical equipment and other systems. The Technician III is also responsible for performing work in accordance with established processes and practices and for complying with internal and external requirements including but not limited to environmental, health and safety, fire protection.

KEY DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Troubleshooting

• Provides observations about facility, facility mechanical and electrical equipment, and systems conditions and deficiencies and provides suggestions for enhancement and repair.

Maintenance

  • Performs work in accordance with established processes and practices.
  • Complies with all internal and external requirements including but not limited to environmental, health and safety, fire protection.
  • Performs regular facility, mechanical and other equipment and systems monitoring inspections, preventative and corrective maintenance to ensure facility uptime objectives are met, uninterrupted client operation and asset integrity of assigned facility are maintained.
  • Responds to routine and on-demand service requests and performs preventative and corrective maintenance on facility mechanical equipment and other systems.
  • Monitors assigned facility by conducting facility walkthroughs for mechanical, electrical, and other equipment system monitoring and inspection.
  • Operates facility mechanical and other systems
  • Manages work order life cycle progressing the work form dispatched through to completion and records resolution data within service maintenance management database. Ensures work completed meets quality, contract response, and all other requirements
  • Assists in the implementation of preventative maintenance (PM) program. Ensures that deficiencies are identified, recorded and escalated, and that related documents are maintained.

Client Relations

  • Assists in enhancing tenant and customer satisfaction and maintaining positive relations through the manner in which work is performed and services delivered.

Administration

  • Participates in and assists with facility-related projects.
  • Ensures the manner in which work is performed is in compliance with corporate and legislated policies, procedures, practices, and guidelines related to environmental, health and safety, fire protection, and any other applicable requirements.
  • Maintains all assigned tools and arranges for repair and replacement where required
  • Submits all expenditures on a timely basis.
  • Other duties as assigned

EDUCATION, JOB-RELATED YEARS OF EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS

  • High school diploma plus trades training and/or certification or licensing.
  • Minimum 3 years experience providing preventive and corrective maintenance on heating ventilation and air conditions systems, or pneumatic or hydraulic systems.
  • Sound knowledge of processes and practices relating to facility operations and maintenance
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain, troubleshoot and repair (as per applicable qualifications) mechanical and other building systems and equipment
  • Possesses a strong environmental, health, and safety mindset.
  • Strong client-service orientation along with a high sense of urgency
  • Knowledge and understanding of Building Automation Systems (BAS)
  • Knowledge and understanding of HVAC Systems
  • Effective communication skills for the purpose of data relay, exchange, feedback, and clarification

title: Lab Assistant (Research Lab Tech I)
location: Los Angeles, CA - University Park Campus
description:
We’re recruiting a full-time lab tech to join the Shared Minds Lab at the University of Southern California! This is a great opportunity for someone looking to gain hands-on research experience before pursuing a PhD in neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology, or a related field.

The Shared Minds Lab, led by PI Sam Nastase at USC (), is accepting applications for a full-time lab tech/research assistant to begin in Fall 2026.

This will be an fMRI-forward position centered on intensive, naturalistic neuroimaging paradigms for language, conversation, and social-narrative videogame play. The lab manager will play a central role in coordinating with participants and leading fMRI data collection across multiple related projects.

Beyond data collection, there will be opportunities to get involved in fMRI data analysis and computational modeling, particularly using large language models (LLMs) to study naturalistic language and social interaction. This position is well suited to someone interested in gaining experience with human neuroscience research while developing the computational skills that will make you a strong candidate for graduate school.

The lab assistant will:

Coordinate participant recruitment, screening, scheduling, and study logistics

Lead fMRI data collection for multiple related naturalistic neuroimaging studies

Maintain research documentation, participant records, and data organization

Contribute to data analysis and modeling depending on experience and interests

We’re looking for someone who is organized, reliable, communicative, and excited about research.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology, or a related field
  • Strong organizational and interpersonal skills with careful attention to detail
  • Experience with fMRI and/or programming (e.g. Python) is a plus, but is not required

The Shared Minds Lab studies how we communicate our thoughts to one another in real-world settings, with an emphasis on natural language, narrative, and social interaction. Our work combines neuroimaging with computational approaches for modeling rich, real-world stimuli and behavior. The lab manager will work closely with collaborators in the Phonetics and Phonology group, the Signal Analysis and Interpretation Laboratory (SAIL), and the Brain and Creativity Institute at USC, as well as collaborators in industry.

The opportunity:

An exciting opportunity has arisen within the Portfolio Systems team to lead the delivery of the Engineering Design Record (EDR) and associated activities.

This is a high visibility, stakeholder rich role with an opportunity to influence and shape one of the key engineering activities across the UK Portfolio. You’ll work with a broad range of stakeholders across multiple projects, navigating a fast-paced environment while delivering tangible outputs to MBDA and MOD. This role offers an excellent opportunity to challenge yourself, lead a small team and packages of work, broaden your strategic understanding and build a deeper understanding of MBDA and MOD business practices, whilst developing your knowledge of MBDA’s products and the wider Portfolio.

The Portfolio Management Team (PMT) provides a leading role in evolving the way MBDA develops and delivers our products in a joint environment with MOD. The Portfolio seeks to provide greater levels of capability within the UK budget, with increased UK sovereign control and better value for money than our competitors.

The Portfolio Systems team supports the development of the engineering coherence through Commonality, Modularity and Reuse across the UK Portfolio of Complex Weapons - current and future - by managing and delivery of the Portfolio Engineering Design Record (EDR). This includes engaging with senior stakeholders across the business to define, agree and verify the Portfolio requirements on Programmes, Equipment Teams, Centres of Excellence and Functional teams.

The role will allow the individual to influence the direction of travel and broaden their skillset through a range of supporting Systems Team work packages; such as Intellectual Property, Test & Evaluation Facilities, MBDA Supplier Databases, Systems Studies exploring technical trades-offs, etc.

There will be opportunities to develop and lead junior colleagues and present your work at the Joint MOD/MBDA Portfolio Engineering Working group as well as travel within the UK to other MBDA sites. The successful individual will also get exposure and opportunities to support wider Portfolio factors such as platform integration, financial efficiencies, operational performance, exportability, obsolescence and Freedom of Action to the UK MOD.

What we're looking for from you:

  • A general understanding of weapon systems, missile systems and design process throughout a product’s life cycle.
  • Is comfortable engaging with multiple stakeholders and building effective working relationships across the Portfolio enterprise and the wider business.
  • Ability to lead and motivate small teams, including developing and empowering junior colleagues.
  • Ability to work with, influence, and where required, challenge senior MOD and MBDA management.
  • A flexible mindset, able to tackle problems and develop genuinely innovative solutions for a given challenge.
  • An ability to take a big picture view and then select the key tactical issues to focus in on.
  • Knowledge of Systems Engineering approaches and practices, ideally familiar with using DOORS, and in particular requirement management.
  • Ability to develop and work a System Design / Requirement Trade, including requirement acceptance with stakeholders.
  • Ability to operate with autonomy and effectively manage their priorities when presented with issues from multiple stakeholders.

Our company: Peace is not a given, Freedom is not a given, Sovereignty is not a given

MBDA is a leading defence organisation. We are proud of the role we play in supporting the Armed Forces who protect our nations. We partner with governments to work together towards a common goal, defending our freedom.

We are proud of our employee-led networks, examples include: Gender Equality, Pride, Menopause Matters, Parents and Carers, Armed Forces, Ethnic Diversity, Neurodiversity, Disability and more…

We recognise that everyone is unique, and we encourage you to speak to us should you require any advice, support or adjustments throughout our recruitment process.

title: Director, Investigations - Crypto Exam and Regulatory Conduct
description:
The Director of the Crypto Fraud & Market Abuse team is responsible for leading a highly skilled team of investigators that focus on detection, investigation and mitigation of crypto-related fraud and market abuse within the securities industry.

The Director of the Crypto Fraud & Market Abuse team oversees the end-to-end execution of investigations related to crypto-related fraud and market abuse that require a range of onchain investigative techniques - including onchain research and analysis, blockchain analytics and forensics, smart contract auditing – as well as traditional investigative techniques such as review and assessment of open source intelligence, data analysis and analytics and the review of books and records.

The Director of the Crypto Fraud & Market Abuse team oversees initiatives focused on mitigation of crypto-fraud and market abuse threats within the securities industry, including engagement and intelligence sharing initiatives with member firms, regulatory partners, law enforcement and internal and external stakeholders.

The Director of the Crypto Fraud & Market Abuse serves as a subject matter expert for FINRA on crypto-related fraud and market abuse within the securities industry, providing guidance strategic support to Investigations leadership, assisting in the development and delivery of training for FINRA staff and member firms, and speaking at industry and FINRA sponsored events to raise awareness of priority and emerging threats and effective practices for member firms to consider as part of their risk-based compliance programs.

The Director of the Crypto Fraud & Market Abuse maintains and cultivates team expertise in cryptocurrency, tokenization, blockchains and other onchain technologies as well as crypto asset compliance to address complex regulatory challenges; foundational knowledge includes familiarity with fraud schemes, money laundering tactics, and other threat vectors in the crypto space, including on/offchain vulnerabilities.

Essential Job Functions:

  • Lead & Manage Investigations — Provide leadership, oversight, direction, and active day-to-day management of a team of investigators handling a set of misconduct matters; ensure investigations are thorough, strategically sound, and supported by clear and sufficient evidence using accepted and reliable methodologies; and provide guidance on investigative strategy.
  • Drive Timely Case Resolution — Monitor case progress, aging, and staff caseloads; identify and correct caseload imbalances; prioritize high-risk and high-priority matters and ensure effective and efficient resolution.
  • Review & Approve Work Product — Review and approve investigative findings, analyses, reports, dispositions, investigative summaries, and referrals to enforcement and external entities, ensuring all written work product is high-quality, professional, and persuasive.
  • Identify, Escalate & Resolve Regulatory Issues — Proactively identify and escalate regulatory issues, novel fact patterns, programmatic risks, emerging market trends, and management needs; develop and advocate for potential solutions in partnership with the Senior Director.
  • Foster Cross-Functional Collaboration — Build and maintain effective working relationships with Enforcement and other RegOps partners; facilitate active information-sharing and a coordinated approach to investigations and regulatory outcomes.
  • Develop People & Build Team Capability — Mentor, coach, and develop staff through performance feedback, training opportunities, and targeted assignments; monitor performance and ensure the team has the needed resources to support continuous improvement; and foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and open dialogue.
  • Support Program Strategy & Continuous Improvement — Lead and participate in developing and implementing program strategy, including business process improvements, technology enhancements, and resource allocation; initiate or recommend thematic reviews, sweeps, and other program initiatives; take initiative in identifying and advancing improvements that strengthen investigative execution and regulatory outcomes.
  • Represent FINRA Externally — Engage professionally with external regulators and agencies, and member firms; facilitate responses to oversight and access requests; represent FINRA at relevant industry events and stakeholder meetings.
  • Demonstrate FINRA’s values.
  • Collaboration, both in-person and virtually, in furtherance of FINRA’s mission of investor protection and market integrity.

Education/Experience Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. Advanced degree (MBA, JD) or professional certification (e.g., CFE, ACAMS, CPA) strongly preferred.
  • Minimum of ten (10) years of progressive experience in the securities, financial services, or financial regulatory industry, with substantive knowledge of regulatory compliance.
  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience providing guidance to staff, and leading projects and initiatives, in an investigative, examination, or enforcement team environment.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting or overseeing enforcement-oriented or regulatory investigations of varying complexity.
  • Familiarity with investigative technologies, data analysis tools, and data strategies.
  • FINRA Securities Industry Essentials (SIE) certification or acceptable industry equivalent certification is required upon hire or within 16 months of the start date of the assigned SIE training cohort.

Knowledge Requirements:

  • Expert knowledge of relevant FINRA rules, applicable SRO rules, the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and federal securities laws, with responsibility for staying current on regulatory rules, practices, and developments and ensuring the team does the same.
  • Substantive knowledge of securities markets, member firm operations, books and records, and firm business models, products, and services relative to the area(s) of misconduct.
  • Comprehensive understanding of regulatory compliance issues and the risks associated with firm business lines and customer bases.
  • Awareness of industry events, emerging trends, and regulatory developments pertinent to the area(s) of misconduct.
  • Familiarity with FINRA's organizational structure, departmental mandates, and cross-functional and cross-organizational priorities, with the ability to apply that understanding to stakeholder engagement and investigative decision-making.

Skills Requirements:

  • Leadership: Expert ability to build trust, align high-performing teams around common objectives, empower direct reports while exercising sound judgment, and foster a culture of accountability, innovation, open dialogue, and continuous improvement.
  • Investigative Judgment: Demonstrated ability to assess investigative strategy, interpret results of data analysis and investigative tools, make sound decisions, and progress complex matters to resolution.
  • Communication: Highly advanced written and verbal communication skills, including outstanding interpersonal, presentation, and stakeholder engagement skills; ability to communicate effectively with staff in multiple geographic locations and represent FINRA professionally with external parties.
  • Collaboration: Expert ability to liaise effectively with internal and external stakeholders; proactively build networks across RegOps and partner organizations; exercise sound judgment in determining when and how to engage, including when the Director's presence is needed in stakeholder meetings.
  • Prioritization & Organization: Highly advanced organizational skills with excellent attention to detail; ability to manage multiple time-sensitive matters simultaneously and balance tactical execution with strategic direction.
  • Risk Identification: Expert ability to identify, prioritize, and escalate risk; recognize priority matters and advocate professionally to drive timely and foreseeable outcomes.
  • People Development: Demonstrated ability to provide meaningful coaching, training, and development opportunities; seek and incorporate feedback from key stakeholders to continuously improve team performance.
  • Initiative & Management Awareness: Demonstrated ability to be proactive, take initiative, anticipate management needs, respond with accountability and follow-through, and help drive timely solutions.

Working Conditions:

  • Hybrid work environment with defined in-person presence requirements.
  • Extended hours and some travel may be required.

Job Responsibilities

  • Communicates with patients, families, physicians, clinical staff, and insurance companies to obtain information and insurance verification to ensure quality patient care and payment of hospital accounts.

  • Coordinates subpoena process between court system, Child Protection Center, and legal department and facilitates billing process for expert testimony in court cases (clinic setting/Center for Safe and Healthy Children).
